items.synopsis: A short French clip framing a new Elegoo machine as strong enough to worry Bambu Lab, the current reference in consumer FDM printing. items.synopsis: The caption announces the release of Gemini Embeddings 2 and nothing more, tagged for RAG and programming audiences. No dimensions, benchmark scores, pricing or migration notes are given. The details are only in the video.

The walkthrough by Florian Burnel targets the exact concern that makes dictation risky at work, namely sending voice data to a third party, and shows a fully offline setup instead. The written guide is linked in the caption for anyone wanting to reproduce it.
items.author: it_connect.fr

items.title: Apple spends 2 billion dollars on silent-speech technology
items.synopsis: The post reports Apple buying Israeli startup Q.ai for around two billion dollars, its second-biggest acquisition ever, founded by the person behind Face ID. The technology reads micro-movements in the face to infer what someone is thinking or whispering, pointing at an interface that needs no spoken word. The creator frames it as either peak convenience or the end of privacy, and uses it to funnel viewers to a free WhatsApp community.

items.title: A local AI dubbing app running entirely on a Raspberry Pi 5
items.synopsis: Part one of a project building an AI dubbing application that runs fully offline on a Raspberry Pi 5, supplied by Kubii France. The creator walks through the three building blocks in turn, speech-to-text, translation and text-to-speech, then covers installing and configuring the stack on the Pi itself. It is a concrete demonstration that a usable dubbing pipeline fits on single-board hardware.
items.author: poparchitecte

items.title: A million AI words for five dollars, and what is left for humans
items.synopsis: The creator contrasts human output of 16,000-20,000 spoken words a day with an AI generating around a million words for roughly five dollars, and notes that price keeps falling toward cents. His conclusion is that once knowledge becomes nearly free, competing on volume or typing speed is hopeless. The only defensible ground left is being human: real stories, real feelings, lived experience.
items.author: santiagoguyfilms

items.title: Fresh layoffs flagged in finance and investment banking
items.synopsis: A short clip claiming another round of job cuts is coming to the financial sector and investment banking. The caption offers no bank names, numbers or sources, and the AI connection is implied only through hashtags. The substance sits entirely in the video.
items.author: shashank_udupa

items.title: Inside the NVLink Spine of NVIDIA GB200 racks
items.synopsis: The post details the NVLink Spine at the centre of the NVIDIA GB200 system: roughly 130 terabytes per second moving across 72 GPUs through about 5,000 precision-made cables. Nine switches let every GPU address every other simultaneously, removing the bottlenecks that would otherwise throttle trillion-parameter training. The framing is that this cabling, not the headlines, is what makes current frontier models physically possible.
items.author: wealthy.college

items.title: DeepSeek OCR and the push for more effective tokens
items.synopsis: The creator breaks down a DeepSeek research paper introducing a new OCR approach aimed at extracting more value per token. The argument is that representing documents visually lets a model carry the same information in far fewer tokens, which directly cuts context cost. He invites discussion rather than selling a tool.
items.author: alex_intelligence_

items.title: Bypassing the Windows 11 hardware requirements
items.synopsis: A repair-shop account teases a method to install Windows 11 on hardware that fails the official TPM and CPU checks. The caption is a bare title followed by PC-repair hashtags, with no steps, tool names or caveats. The actual method is only in the video.

items.title: Vocal Remover strips the instrumental out of any track
items.synopsis: The post demonstrates vocalremover.org, a browser tool that separates a song into vocal and instrumental stems. The creator names the exact site in the caption because Instagram captions are not clickable, so the tool is directly reproducible. It is aimed at anyone needing an a cappella or karaoke version without audio software.
items.author: marieelenasrn

items.title: Ai-Da, the humanoid robot that makes its own art decisions
items.synopsis: France Info profiles Ai-Da, a humanoid robot artist whose synthetic skin conceals eight computers, two cameras and a robotic arm. It was built by a former gallerist working with engineers, with the explicit goal of a machine that observes its surroundings and takes artistic decisions on its own. The piece frames Ai-Da as a genuine disruption to the art world rather than a novelty.
items.author: franceinfo

items.title: Mistral Vibe 2.0 brings per-task sub-agents to coding
items.synopsis: The post presents Mistral Vibe 2.0 as a change in how you code, built around sub-agents dedicated to individual tasks. items.title: Quantization as the quiet revolution behind AI chips
items.synopsis: The creator introduces quantization as one of the biggest revolutions in AI and explains it in the video. He ties it directly to the dedicated AI processors now reaching the market, naming the Apple Neural Engine and the forthcoming Tesla AI5 as hardware built to exploit it. The caption establishes the link between the technique and the silicon without walking through the mechanics.

items.title: ChatGPT secrets, part thirty-seven
items.synopsis: The thirty-seventh instalment of a ChatGPT tips series, with a caption consisting only of the series title and hashtags. No tip, prompt or feature is stated in the text. The content is video-only.

items.author: jeremy_ia

items.title: Which video model to use for which job, five options compared
items.synopsis: The creator maps five video generators to distinct use cases in a single pass. Sora 2 is put forward for UGC-style video, Kling 2.5 for cinematic work and Veo 3.1 as the all-in-one powerhouse. Wan 2.5 is named for uncensored 4K output and Seedance for anime and stylised ads, with links gated behind commenting AI.
items.author: theaisurfer

items.title: Three disciplines before AI creative work pays
items.synopsis: The creator argues you cannot earn with AI until three things are mastered, and that chasing trends is what keeps most creators poor while systems are what clients pay thousands for. First is consistency across product, character and brand, generating the same subject a hundred times without variation, because clients buy reliability. Second is prompt structure, replacing random prompting with reusable frameworks for repeatable, scalable quality; third is speed, since manual work does not scale and must be automated.
items.author: timkoda_

items.title: Free routes to premium AI tools from Ray 2 to Midjourney
items.synopsis: The post promises free access to premium AI capability spanning image generation and voice cloning, via sites the creator says turn your own computer into an AI workstation with no limits and full privacy. Ray 2 and Midjourney are named as examples of what becomes reachable from one place. All links are gated behind commenting AI.
items.author: theaisurfer

items.title: Turning reference images into JSON context profiles for ChatGPT
items.synopsis: The creator shares a technique for generating highly accurate images inside ChatGPT by first converting a reference image into a JSON context profile. Structuring the description as JSON is what makes the subsequent generations consistent rather than approximate. The full prompt is released to anyone commenting Image.
items.author: mavgpt

items.title: AI tooling in 2022 against 2026
items.synopsis: A before-and-after clip contrasting the AI tool landscape of 2022 with 2026. The caption is only a title and hashtags, naming no tool on either side. The comparison exists solely in the video.

items.synopsis: The post presents OpenApps as a library of free, open-source alternatives to expensive subscription software, spanning AI, DevOps, design and productivity. The apps are organised by category so a paid tool can be swapped for a capable replacement directly. The full list is gated behind commenting OPEN.
items.author: theaisurfer

items.title: One browser platform replacing ten paid AI and document tools
items.synopsis: The creator describes a free site covering AI image and video generation, image-to-video, image-to-prompt, website generation, image editing and background removal in one place. Beyond generation it bundles document utilities for PDF, Excel and Word plus file converters normally sold as paid tools. He stresses there are no signup tricks or hidden limits and everything runs directly in the browser, with the link DMed to anyone commenting AI.

items.title: Une extension Chrome qui réécrit les prompts ChatGPT et Claude en un clic
items.synopsis: L'extension s'installe depuis le Chrome Web Store et n'agit que sur ChatGPT et Claude, où elle ajoute un bouton Optimize Prompt dans l'interface. Un seul clic transforme une saisie brouillonne en prompt structuré, en appliquant des techniques de prompt engineering établies comme l'attribution d'un rôle, l'ajout de contexte et la pose de conditions. Le prompt optimisé reste modifiable avant envoi, et l'auteur réserve le lien de téléchargement à ceux qui commentent extension.

The post is promotional framing around an undisclosed list.
items.author: godofprompt

items.title: A 400-tool AI playground with no signup required
items.synopsis: The creator describes a single site aggregating over four hundred AI tools, covering chat models, image generators and video tools, free to use. Typing a prompt generates unlimited images and videos without creating an account, and uploading a photo allows instant editing of style, outfit or background by description. He calls it an all-in-one AI playground and DMs the link to anyone commenting AI.
items.author: drcintas

items.title: A Character DNA profile that locks identity across prompts
items.synopsis: The creator names the failure everyone hits, where a perfect generated character comes back as a different face on the next prompt and the project dies. His fix is a Character DNA system that pins down height, build, skin tone, face structure, eyes, hair, personality traits, voice tone, speech rhythm, style, posture and expression in one profile fed to the model. With the DNA locked, pose, angle and scene can change while the character stays identical, and the full workflow is gated behind commenting DNA.
items.author: timkoda_

items.title: The ChatGPT App Store nobody is talking about
items.synopsis: The creator argues the newly launched ChatGPT App Store is one of the biggest business opportunities in years and is being badly under-discussed. He walks through the new App Store tab, the roughly seventy-five applications already integrated including Photoshop, Slack and Zoom, the simple at-mention integration inside a chat, and centralised purchasing without leaving ChatGPT. With close to 800 million users, he compares the moment to the original App Store launch.
items.author: danyltn

items.synopsis: Le premier site, Prompt Hackers, propose des centaines de prompts prêts à l'emploi couvrant presque tous les domaines, à copier-coller tels quels. Le deuxième, Originality AI, fonctionne en générateur : on saisit un sujet et il produit des prompts sur mesure. Le troisième, Fido.com, renvoie des prompts détaillés conçus pour pousser ChatGPT plus loin, l'auteur envoyant les liens à qui commente Prompt.

Step one generates a base image with a tightly specified subject and locks both face and scene; step two runs it through Nano Banana Pro with his specific realism prompt, which strips the plastic quality so pores appear and texture returns. He stresses that skipping this second step is exactly why most output still looks generated.
items.author: viznfr

items.title: A Custom GPT that writes photography-grade Nano Banana prompts
items.synopsis: The creator built a Custom GPT that converts reference photos into hyper-detailed, photography-level prompts aimed at Nano Banana Pro. Its explicit purpose is fixing the three recurring failures of fake-looking skin, flat lighting and inconsistent faces, for realistic ads and UGC output. The GPT and an accompanying prompt pack are released to anyone commenting AI.

Individual shots can be extracted as high-resolution frames to feed whichever video model you prefer, such as Veo 3 or Kling. He adds an edit noting the free Vision promotion has ended, though a free invideo account still shows which models are currently free to try.
items.author: taylorgreathead

items.title: Dreamina merges Midjourney-style output with Nano Banana control
items.synopsis: The creator presents Dreamina as combining Midjourney and Nano Banana capability in one tool, producing ultra-realistic 4K images with consistent lighting and clean textures. The features he singles out are merging up to six reference images, adjusting pose, lighting and setting through plain prompts, and converting stills into video. He notes 120 free credits a day and discloses the post as paid collaboration, with the link sent by DM to anyone commenting IA.

The contrast drawn is NVIDIA GPUs as versatile but expensive and power-hungry against Google TPUs as specialised, efficient and purpose-built. The decisive claim is that Google built Gemini 3 on these chips and beat GPT-5 benchmarks without touching a single NVIDIA GPU.

The comparison is per-model and motion-focused: Seedance Pro produces very subtle, almost hesitant motion with minimal slow head rotation, reading as mild curiosity rather than reaction. Its stated strength is rock-solid temporal stability, with a fixed steady image and clean, controlled movement.

He positions it for rapid world-building, previs and early Unreal workflows before committing to heavy 3D production, with the link gated behind commenting WORLD.

The trigger is an HSBC report projecting that OpenAI, Oracle largest customer, faces a funding gap of 207 billion dollars by 2030. The fatal link is Oracle dependence on that one customer to service its own commitments.

items.synopsis: Tip fourteen in a French series covers automating the work you hand to ChatGPT so prompts execute on a schedule. items.title: Silicon Valley interest in selecting smarter babies
items.synopsis: A French reflection on embryo selection for intelligence being seriously considered in Silicon Valley, set against the arrival of superintelligence. The creator poses it as a question of what counts as an unworthy parent in 2025 if such choices become available. It is an ethics provocation rather than reporting on a specific company.
items.author: lafabriquedeslivres

items.title: A Google design canvas that generates twenty variations at once
items.synopsis: The creator describes a quietly released Google design tool he frames as Figma with a brain, and free. One idea produced twenty design variations in seconds, and uploading a reference image with the instruction to make it Japanese style had Nano Banana rebuild the concept consistently. Multiple images can be combined on one canvas just by typing the intent, with access pointed at Boards and gated behind commenting that word.
items.author: theinsiders_club

items.title: Flames Blue generates animated sites from a prompt
items.synopsis: The post pitches Flames Blue as an AI design tool that produces professional, non-template websites in seconds, against builders that all output the same generic layouts. The workflow is five steps: describe the site, generate, watch it build a custom layout with clean UI and animations, preview instantly, then deploy live with no coding. The creator reports testing it on a SaaS landing page, and gates the link behind commenting DESIGN.
items.author: nathanhodgson.ai

items.title: The official route to getting your business cited inside ChatGPT
items.synopsis: The creator presents the official guide for listing a business so it surfaces directly in ChatGPT answers, the discipline now called GEO. His argument for urgency is that search behaviour is shifting from Google to ChatGPT and OpenAI actively wants products to appear in responses. The free guide is released to anyone commenting GEO.
items.author: jeremy_ia

items.title: An unnamed site claiming every AI tool for free
items.synopsis: A single sentence asserting that one website gives free access to all the tools. No site, tool or mechanism is named anywhere in the caption. There is nothing verifiable to extract.
items.author: omnifusion.ai

items.title: Tencent AI embeds personalised ads inside the video itself
items.synopsis: The post describes Tencent technology that removes the ad break by placing brands directly into video content using AI and computer vision. If an actor holds a generic coffee cup, the system identifies the object and composites a brand logo onto it in real time. The logo is swapped according to each viewer location and preferences, so two people watching the same scene see different brands.
items.author: hackonomics.ai

items.title: Claude now creates and edits Office files inside the chat
items.synopsis: The post highlights the Claude ability to create and modify Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF files without the user leaving the conversation. The framing is a colleague who now does that work on request, removing the export-edit-reimport loop. It is aimed at office productivity rather than developers.
items.author: carladecoded

items.title: Virtual try-on built from Nano Banana, Higgsfield and Kling
items.synopsis: A tutorial putting a real t-shirt design, inspired by the Elysia chlorotica sea slug, onto a person using a chain of generative tools. The pipeline combines Nano Banana for image work with Higgsfield and KlingAI for motion, producing a digital-fashion try-on. It is a concrete worked example of stacking three services rather than a single-product demo.
items.author: theorocq

items.title: AlterEgo enables silent conversation without implants
items.synopsis: The post presents AlterEgo, a wearable that picks up micro-signals from facial muscles when the user intends to speak, so no sound and no implant are involved. The result is silent conversation plus real-time translation, with responses delivered only to the wearer. The creator reports early tests as already highly accurate and asks who viewers would try it with.
items.author: david_sepahan

items.title: Google Cloud compendium of 601 real-world gen-AI use cases
items.synopsis: The post points to a free Google Cloud resource collecting more than six hundred concrete generative-AI deployments across industries, from product to operations to marketing. The creator frames it as an organised field manual rather than another scattered ideas list, with real deployments and outcomes instead of speculation. Access is gated behind commenting the word AI.
items.author: kyleherbel

items.title: Yann LeCun: text-trained LLMs will not reach human intelligence
items.synopsis: The post summarises the Yann LeCun argument that large language models trained on text alone cannot reach human-level intelligence, because human intelligence develops through touching, building and testing the world. Closing the gap requires real-world interaction: the system must see, move, experiment and adapt the way a child learns cause and effect. LeCun names robotics, perception, memory and curiosity as the necessary breakthroughs.
items.author: infusewithai

items.title: A Stanford study says generative AI is self-destructing
items.synopsis: Responding to follower requests, the creator presents a Stanford study arguing that generative AI is in the process of destroying itself, the model-collapse problem that arises when systems train on their own output. She asks what this means for the models we depend on and what ways out exist, pointing to a fuller write-up on her blog ninonia.com. It is a critical take on data quality rather than a tool review.
items.author: ninon.ia_officiel

items.title: Paid versus free AI tools, with the list behind a DM gate
items.synopsis: The post compares paid AI tools against free alternatives as a starting point for beginners. No tool is actually named in the caption; the list is promised by DM to anyone commenting the word AI. It functions as lead capture rather than a comparison.
items.author: urvvi.patel

items.title: The five-part prompt template OpenAI recommends for ChatGPT 5
items.synopsis: The post lays out the prompt structure OpenAI recommends for ChatGPT 5, with each slot spelled out in French. The five parts are Role (who should speak or act), Task (precisely what to do, such as finding three lesser-known medium-length hikes near San Francisco), Context (constraints and useful facts, like avoiding tourist trails and checking accuracy), Reasoning (how the model should think and validate, cross-checking reliable sources) and Output format. It is directly usable as a reusable scaffold rather than a tip list.
items.author: unefille.ia

items.title: A single meta-prompt to improve every other prompt
items.synopsis: The creator claims one prompt will substantially improve all of a user subsequent prompts. The prompt itself is not in the caption, which redirects to a full video on his YouTube channel. Nothing is reproducible from the post alone.
items.author: paytonbilodeau

items.title: Your children, not you, will be the ones adopting robots
items.synopsis: A two-line French provocation arguing that household robot adoption will come from the next generation rather than from adults today. The only technical hook is a Hugging Face hashtag, with no product or model named. The reasoning is in the video.
items.author: ninon.ia_officiel

items.title: One subscription fronting 100+ models from Claude to Veo 3
items.synopsis: The post pitches a single site replacing twenty-plus separate AI subscriptions by bundling more than a hundred professional models. The caption enumerates them in detail: Claude Opus 4 and Sonnet 4, DeepSeek R1 and V3, Codestral 2501, Phi 4, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Grok 3, Llama 4 Maverick, GPT-4.1 and 4.5 Preview, Qwen3 variants and GPT-4o for reasoning and code. Video generation is covered by Kling v2.1 and v2.0, Veo 2 and Veo 3 and Runway.
items.author: ai.akshu

items.title: Website cloning and AI influencers behind a comment gate
items.synopsis: The post advertises a tool that clones any website and produces explainer videos and AI influencers. No product is named; the link is released only to people who comment the word AI. The caption is pure lead capture.
items.author: harshhhgautam

items.title: A free three-hour AI course requiring no coding
items.synopsis: The creator points to a free AI training aimed at people who cannot code, totalling three hours split into short five-to-ten-minute videos. She flags clearly that the lessons are in English but French subtitles are available. The format is built for progressive viewing rather than a single sitting.
items.author: unefille.ia

items.title: An unnamed progression clip presented as undeniable
items.synopsis: The caption is one line admiring an insane progression, with no subject identified. Nothing indicates which model, capability or timeline is being compared. The content is entirely visual.
items.author: aifortuneclub

items.title: Camera motion controls and Runway Image-to-Video 4.5
items.synopsis: The creator presents a list of the best camera motion controls for improving AI video output. He highlights Runway Image-to-Video 4.5 for smoother camera movement, more realistic motion and cinematic-quality results from a single image, calling the update a significant step for filmmakers, advertisers and creators needing precise control. The prompts and the tool are gated behind commenting AI.
items.author: rourke

items.title: ChatGPT secrets, part thirty-seven
items.synopsis: The thirty-seventh instalment of a ChatGPT tips series, with a caption consisting only of the series title and hashtags. No tip, prompt or feature is stated in the text. The content is video-only.
items.author: socialtypro

items.title: Google Learn Your Way generates personalised courses
items.synopsis: The post covers Learn Your Way, an experimental Google tool that uses AI to build courses tailored to the individual learner. A concept is adapted to the student level and interests, who can then practise through a mind map, an audio version and personalised visuals. The creator frames it as a plausible glimpse of AI-driven education.
items.author: unefille.ia

items.title: Day one of a ten-day AI basics series from a Stanford engineer
items.synopsis: Harper Carroll opens her most-requested series, Ten Days of AI Basics, with the distinction between AI and machine learning. She establishes her credentials: bachelor and master degrees in computer science and artificial intelligence from Stanford, where she was a teaching assistant on several courses including the PhD-level Decision Making Under Uncertainty. She also spent four years at Facebook and Meta as an AI and ML engineer.
items.author: harpercarrollai

items.title: Claude legal plugin: a 24/7 free law firm
items.synopsis: The reel promotes a new Claude plugin that acts like having a law firm at your fingertips, available 24/7 and completely free. The creator claims it can replace lawyers for everyday legal needs. An installation video is sent to viewers who comment 'LÉGAL'.
items.author: levibecodeur

items.title: A slide generator pitched as better than PowerPoint
items.synopsis: The creator claims this AI slide generator is substantially better than PowerPoint and discloses the post as a paid collaboration. The product is not named in the caption; the link is sent to anyone commenting IA. Only the category is identifiable from the text.
items.author: antony_nonis

items.title: Open-source candlestick forecaster replaces a $24k Bloomberg feature
items.synopsis: An open-source model trained directly on candlestick movement from 45 global exchanges forecasts the estimated path of price, and it already sits on GitHub with roughly 30,000 stars. You hand it a price chart and it returns a forecast range with its uncertainty laid out, rather than a single point guess. The pitch is that forecasting which previously required a Bloomberg terminal at $24,000 a year now runs on an ordinary laptop for nothing, with the usage guide gated behind a 'comment forecast' DM.
items.author: jesserurka

items.title: Claude Code drives TradingView for automated trading
items.synopsis: This French tutorial shows how to connect Claude Code directly to TradingView to automate trading analysis. It walks through installing the application, using GitHub for the configuration, and then issuing natural-language commands to the AI. Demonstrated tasks include drawing liquidity grabs, applying Wyckoff models, and coding custom indicators.
items.author: cryptoedgeofficiel

items.title: An enthusiastic Claude capability clip behind a guide gate
items.synopsis: The creator reacts to Claude performing strongly and asks whether viewers have tried any of the demonstrated capabilities, crediting another account for the material. The caption names no specific feature or workflow. A guide is offered to anyone commenting CLAUDE.
items.author: baroobi.inc

items.title: Claude driving Blender through MCP after Fusion 360
items.synopsis: Following the official Fusion 360 connection, the creator wired Claude to Blender over the MCP protocol. The result is that an object described in natural language is executed directly inside Blender, with no manual modelling step. It is a concrete MCP integration for 3D work rather than a concept demo.
items.author: co_ben_

items.title: Agent Reach gives Claude Code web access without any API
items.synopsis: Agent Reach is a free tool at around 90,000 GitHub stars — up more than 30,000 in the past month — that lets Claude read the internet without paying for a single API, including gated platforms such as LinkedIn, YouTube, Twitter and Instagram. Installation is one line pasted into Claude Code, after which it installs itself. It pulls YouTube transcripts so Claude can scan a competitor's last ten videos in a single pass, strips the clutter from any web page into clean text, and follows feeds, Discords and open-source projects with no login required.
items.author: seymourofdevin

items.title: Claudex Loop pairs Claude Code with Codex for plan-then-build review
items.synopsis: Claudex Loop is a free, open-source skill that wires Claude Code and Codex into a single workflow so the two models check each other's work. Fable 5.1 drafts the implementation plan, GPT-6 Astra challenges it before any code is written, Claude revises the plan, Astra builds it, and Claude then reviews the result against the original requirements. The pitch is fewer mistakes and far less copy-pasting between two separate AI chats, with one model handling the reasoning and the other the engineering.
items.author: thevibefounder

items.title: Claude plus a trending GitHub scraper, tested on real French lead generation
items.synopsis: The tool — the week's number one trending GitHub project — lets Claude search the web or walk through business directories, collect publicly listed contact details and return them as a clean table. The creator tests it properly rather than just demoing it, asking for transport companies in the Oise département to pitch a fleet-management app; after roughly half an hour Claude returns company name, city, director's name, website, email and phone, which he spot-checks and finds accurate. His verdict is that it is not bullshit, though the caption adds a pointed GDPR warning about what you then do with the list.
items.author: justezaki_

items.title: Running Qwen3.8 locally through Ollama and Hermes Desktop
items.synopsis: The walkthrough shows how to run the popular Qwen3.8 model locally with Ollama rather than the more commonly used LM Studio. It covers installing Ollama, pulling the 27B model from either the terminal or the desktop UI, then launching Hermes Desktop against it and selecting the model. A fallback path configures a custom Ollama endpoint in Hermes settings, and the host notes that uncensored variants realistically need 64 GB of memory or more.
items.author: codrkai

items.title: 100+ shorthand ChatGPT image prompts, gated behind a comment
items.synopsis: A rapid before/after reel cycling through image results, each narrated only as type this, get this against a shorthand prompt. Neither the caption nor the audio names a technique, model setting or reasoning, so the whole post works as a delivery hook for a pack of 100+ ChatGPT image prompts sent by DM on comment. The visible outputs suggest short keyword-style prompts for stylised images, but nothing in the post is specific enough to reconstruct.
items.author: farhannrakhangi

items.title: The 10 Claude Code skills that change the most, plus how to write your own
items.synopsis: Ben argues Claude Code gets far more useful once you stop re-explaining your method every session, and that a skill is nothing more than a folder holding one text file describing that method. The carousel ranks the ten skills he considers highest-impact, from searching a large codebase to a meta-skill that writes new skills for you. The linked 11-page guide adds what the carousel cannot hold: the exact trigger phrase for each skill, the two real install commands, a complete SKILL.md to copy, and the three usual reasons a skill fails to fire.
items.author: bencodezero

items.title: A developer open-sources a 10-month Claude Code setup: 286 skills, 68 sub-agents
items.synopsis: Eric walks through a GitHub user's Claude Code configuration built over ten months of live production work and then released publicly, containing 286 skills, 68 sub-agents and a security scanner originally written at an Anthropic hackathon. Rather than one general agent, the setup routes each job to a purpose-built sub-agent: one writes the feature, another reviews it, another runs 102 security checks looking for leaks. A plain-markdown memory vault on the local machine carries context across days and across tools into Codex, and the setup watches finished sessions and converts what worked into new skills automatically.
items.author: erictechpro

items.title: Plugging Meta Ads into Claude as a custom MCP connector
items.synopsis: Madame T3ch demonstrates adding a Facebook/Meta Ads MCP server to Claude as a custom connector, pasting the server link under the connector settings so Claude can create ads, run campaigns and read the account statistics directly. She then prompts it to surface ad trends in the week's data that she would not have found manually, with Claude pulling straight from the live ad account. The second half chains the Higgsfield MCP to generate ten static ads from an imported product and push them into a Meta Ads campaign, recommending Seedance 2.5 when the creative should be video instead of stills.
items.author: madamet3ch

items.title: Ten open-source repos worth 500,000 GitHub stars for Claude Code users
items.synopsis: Neej rounds up ten repositories that collectively hold over half a million GitHub stars, framed around what each adds to a Claude Code session. The coding-focused entries include GSD, which runs a build as a spec-driven loop that survives long sessions, graphify, which turns a codebase into a knowledge graph so the model stops re-reading files, and an official OpenAI plugin putting Codex inside Claude Code for second opinions on diffs. The rest span design and media tooling: diagram-design and impeccable against AI design slop, scroll-world for 3D landing pages, cap as an open-source Loom, MoneyPrinterTurbo for vertical video, the xAI For You ranking code, and Block's buzz for agents in team chat.
items.author: buildwithneej

items.title: Audit your Instagram audience with Claude via MCP
items.synopsis: A walkthrough of connecting an Instagram account to Claude through an MCP server to pull a full audience breakdown. The creator pastes a single growth prompt and lets Claude analyse follower composition and engagement patterns. The output is a custom growth strategy generated in under five minutes.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Six GitHub repos to turn into paid AI services
items.synopsis: A carousel arguing that GitHub holds free tools capable of auditing ads, generating AI content, automating research and producing video at scale. The pitch is not reselling the code but packaging these open-source tools into billable services and workflows. Named repos include Claude Ads and Fincept Terminal, each with a suggested commercial angle.
items.author: techskills

items.title: Anthropic's free pack of 11 role-based plugins for Claude
items.synopsis: Anthropic released eleven first-party plugins that preload Claude with a working setup for a specific business function — sales, marketing, finance, support and so on down the line. Each plugin arrives already knowing how that role operates and wired into the tools that role uses day to day, so you install once instead of re-explaining what a good marketing brief or clean financial summary looks like every session. The demonstrated payoff: drop in the sales plugin and Claude can research a prospect and draft the outreach; use the finance one to pull numbers into a report.
items.author: aifornontechies

items.title: ChatGPT as a personal beauty and grooming consultant
items.synopsis: The creator shares a prompt that turns ChatGPT into a personal image consultant. A user uploads a clear photo and receives tailored feedback on facial features, hairstyle and grooming. The analysis extends to skincare suggestions and overall look.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Everything Claude Code: 64 agents and 261 skills in one repo
items.synopsis: A single GitHub repo, Everything Claude Code, has passed 240,000 stars and was built by the winner of an Anthropic hackathon. It bundles 64 specialised agents, 261 skills and 84 commands and hooks that fire automatically, installable in one command and free. The creator's summary is that Claude stops being an assistant that answers and becomes a full team.
items.author: henriexploria

items.title: Lumen: a seven-agent crew that runs a YouTube channel
items.synopsis: Lumen is a free AI agent system that takes a YouTube channel end to end, from idea to publication. Seven agents split the work: trend analysis and content strategy, scripts with hooks and calls to action, thumbnail generation and A/B testing, SEO on titles and keywords, production covering voice and visuals and editing, then scheduling and publishing. The seventh is the differentiator, analysing performance after each video and feeding the data back to the whole crew.
items.author: simon_de_lima

items.title: DeepSeek Harness: build local AI agents from plugins
items.synopsis: The DeepSeek Harness is an MIT-licensed open-source project, at 172,000 stars, for building your own AI agents locally. Installation is a single command after Node, opening a full dashboard in the browser, and everything runs on your machine so your data stays local. Its architecture is plugin-based, so capabilities are snapped together to shape the agent.
items.author: kacperrutkai

items.title: xAI Voice Agents let AI place real phone calls
items.synopsis: xAI Voice Agents move AI agents from messaging into placing actual phone calls, configured by describing the desired behaviour in plain language. You choose the script and voice, get a phone number, and test before calling for real. A real-time speech-to-speech pipeline keeps latency low and can switch languages mid-conversation, targeting lead qualification and appointment booking.
items.author: thevibefounder

items.title: CLI-anything lets Claude Code generate a CLI for almost any application
items.synopsis: The creator's point is that Claude Code is at its most powerful when it drives other applications, which normally requires an MCP or an existing CLI — so what happens when the software has neither. CLI-anything is a GitHub repo that lets Claude Code build a CLI for essentially any software you use, and it comes from the makers of LightRAG and RAG-Anything rather than an unknown author. It has already been used to generate CLIs for GIMP, Blender, Audacity, Inkscape, n8n, and Mailchimp among many others.
items.author: chase.h.ai

items.title: Claude's Skill Recorder turns a narrated screen recording into an automation
items.synopsis: The creator demonstrates Claude's new Skill Recorder feature, which captures a screen recording while the user narrates what they are doing and points at the interface elements involved. Claude interprets that demonstration to infer the underlying process and then proposes a way to automate it. The video walks through the recording workflow end to end in French.
items.author: elliottpierret

items.title: Hermes Agent skill derives reusable API access by watching browser requests
items.synopsis: Automating legacy business software without a public API has traditionally forced AI to pilot the interface like a human — screenshot, locate the button, click, screenshot again. This new Hermes Agent skill changes the approach: you demonstrate an operation in the browser and it observes the underlying network requests, then derives a reusable, far lighter access path than replaying the whole navigation. The creator notes it bypasses neither authentication nor permissions — your account, rights, and the software's protections still apply.
items.author: nicodecode

items.title: Prime Agent enters the arena as a free, self-improving open-source agent
items.synopsis: Prime Agent is presented as a new entrant in the AI agent space built around one central idea: self-improvement. It is free and open source, running autonomous loops designed to keep working, iterating, and refining its approach to a task. The creator frames it as serious competition for Hermes Agent.
items.author: julian.goldie_

items.title: FYI agent V2 will call you instead of waiting to be asked
items.synopsis: FYI previews V2 of its agentic building platform, where the agent can proactively phone the user rather than only responding to prompts. Users set reminders and choose topics they want to stay on top of, and the agent checks in, delivers a debrief, and keeps the conversation moving. The pitch is a shift from question-answering toward systems that work around the user's schedule.
items.author: fyi.ai

items.title: Agent Reach gives an AI agent live access to 15+ platforms
items.synopsis: Agent Reach connects an AI assistant to more than fifteen platforms — YouTube, Reddit, Twitter/X, GitHub, LinkedIn, RSS feeds and others — so it can search, read, and summarize live content instead of guessing. Some channels work instantly with zero setup while others need a one-time login. The demo shows it pulling a live YouTube summary, scraping trending posts, and analyzing a real job posting against the creator's resume; it is free and open source.
items.author: thetechniko

items.title: An entire AI agency open-sourced: 147 agents across 12 departments
items.synopsis: Someone has published a complete AI agency on GitHub, comprising 147 agents organized into twelve departments. The departments cover engineering, marketing, sales, support, product, and more, all structured to operate like a real company team. The post frames it as a ready-made multi-agent organizational template.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Six AI releases in 60 seconds: Pocket TTS, Hermes Skills Hub, Grok Imagine 2.0, Muse Code, Qwen3.8-Max, Kimi K3 in C
items.synopsis: This rapid weekly roundup covers Kyutai's Pocket TTS (a 100M-parameter voice model that clones a voice locally at 6x realtime from one command), Nous Research's Hermes Skills Hub (90,000+ free community skills across 200 categories), and xAI's Grok Imagine Image 2.0 with regional editing and five simultaneous references. It continues with Meta's first coding agent Muse Code, which keeps background agents alive across a session and works the repo in parallel worktrees, and Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Max at 2.4 trillion parameters with a 1M-token context window. Topping the list is kimi-k3-in-c, a 176 KB pure C99 engine that streams Kimi K3's experts off disk rather than loading them into memory.
items.author: drcintas

items.title: Prime Agent lifts Claude Opus 5 from 30% to 95.5% on a reasoning benchmark
items.synopsis: The creator argues that using AI means using two things — the model as the brain, and the scaffolding around it that governs memory and organisation — and that everyone fixates on the brain. Prime Agent is a free open-source harness pluggable onto any model, and on a well-known logic benchmark human experts score 95% and Claude Opus 5 alone scores 30%, while Claude Opus 5 running on Prime Agent reaches 95.5%. Its key behaviour is refusing to swallow an entire project the way a coding agent does before losing the thread, instead putting the file down and pulling only what is relevant at that moment.
items.author: simon_de_lima

items.title: A seven-agent AI content team run by one creator
items.synopsis: The creator replaced a manual content workflow with seven specialised AI agents, each owning a single job. The roster covers a researcher for trends and competitors, a hook writer, a script writer, a designer, an analyst, a manager and a publisher. The carousel lays out how the agents hand off to one another across the full content pipeline.
items.author: seb.ai

items.title: Wan2GP runs open-source AI video on a 6GB GPU
items.synopsis: Wan2GP is an open-source AI video generator built for people without cloud subscriptions or high-end hardware. It targets consumer GPUs, needing only about 6GB of VRAM to run. That puts it in reach of most mid-range NVIDIA cards from the past eight years.
items.author: karthikramaniai

items.title: HyperResearch adds a deep research loop to Claude Code
items.synopsis: HyperResearch is an open-source tool layering a structured research workflow on top of Claude Code. Rather than a single search it decomposes a question into multiple tasks, searches several angles at once and weighs conflicting sources instead of taking the first answer. It then drafts a report and runs multiple self-critique passes, retaining prior research so later reports build on it.
items.author: thevibefounder

items.title: Atomic Agent: Local Open-Source Computer-Use Agent
items.synopsis: Atomic Agent is presented as an open-source AI agent that automates real computer tasks entirely on your own machine. It can plan multi-step workflows, browse the web, edit files, run terminal commands, and keep memory across tasks without sending data to the cloud. The GitHub link is available to anyone commenting "AGENT".
items.author: aiadventureryt

items.title: Hermès agent remembers you across sessions
items.synopsis: The reel presents Hermès, an AI agent that keeps persistent memory of the user, their projects, and past sessions. It builds a growing library of skills from those sessions, so the assistant improves over time instead of starting fresh. The creator frames this as the future of agents and shows when and how to use it.
items.author: 0xloucash

items.title: Postiz: self-hosted social scheduling with an agent CLI
items.synopsis: Postiz is an open-source social media manager at roughly 30,000 GitHub stars that schedules posting across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and LinkedIn from one calendar. What Buffer cannot match is its agent CLI: you point Claude at it and tell it to schedule a week, and it drafts and queues the posts without opening a dashboard. Analytics, AI writing and a public API for n8n, Make or Zapier are included, and the self-hosted build is feature-complete and free.
items.author: brodyautomates

items.title: A copy-paste loop library for Claude and Codex agents
items.synopsis: The creator shares a library of agent loops usable with both Claude and Codex. You copy and paste it in, and the agent takes care of setting up the loop best suited to your project. The clip is a short French tip aimed at terminal-based coding agents.
items.author: 0xloucash

items.title: An open-source WhatsApp API gateway that skips Meta's approval process
items.synopsis: The creator celebrates someone finally publishing an open-source API gateway for WhatsApp that you can set up on your own computer. Its appeal is avoiding what he calls the excruciating process of obtaining API access through Meta. It is fully open source and completely free.
items.author: mahanaicoach

items.title: A five-install stack that gives Claude Code memory, taste and a browser
items.synopsis: The creator runs through installing five upgrades into Claude Code in sequence, each by pasting a link. He starts with Claude Mem from GitHub for memory, then the Taste skill so it stops generating AI slop, then Impeccable for better front-end design. He finishes with design motion principles for interactive components and animations, plus an agent browser he rates above Playwright.
items.author: zayluiss

items.title: NotebookLM + Hermes as a 24/7 research agent
items.synopsis: The reel shows how NotebookLM can power an AI agent when paired with Hermes. Together they form a 24/7 research system described as a researcher on call who never sleeps. The creator claims this unlocks capabilities most people don't know exist and shares the full video via comment.
items.author: jackroberts___

items.title: ScrapeGraph AI does in free what Apify and Bright Data charge for
items.synopsis: An Italian developer released ScrapeGraph AI under an MIT licence, free forever, and it has already gathered 23,000 stars. You give it a URL and describe what you want in plain English, and the AI handles the rest — LinkedIn profiles, email addresses, Twitter accounts, Amazon, Zillow, Glassdoor — including multi-page scraping at scale. The creator's economic point is that Apify charges $49 a month and Bright Data $500, while agencies are already billing clients $5,000 per scraping project using this free tool.
items.author: criscatalyst

items.title: Nano Banana generates coherent never-photographed images
items.synopsis: The reel showcases photorealistic images of scenes that were never photographed, generated entirely from a single prompt. The creator stresses there is no retouching or compositing, with Nano Banana handling everything. An 'ultimate Nano Banana guide' is offered to viewers who comment NANO.
items.author: jeremy_ia

items.title: Scrapling: 800x faster scraper that dodges Cloudflare
items.synopsis: A French video promoting Scrapling, a scraper billed as 800 times faster than existing tools, installable in 30 seconds via Claude Code. It reportedly bypasses Cloudflare without detection, enabling claims like 10,000 leads in one night with zero banned IPs. It is presented as compatible with OpenAI Codex and other agent tooling.
items.author: just_use_ai_now

items.title: Higgsfield MCP lets Manus run Instagram on autopilot
items.synopsis: Higgsfield announces that its MCP integration is now available on Manus. Agents can generate top-tier content and post it through Instagram, Meta Ads, and the Creator Marketplace. The stack bundles Seedance 2.0, GPT Images 2.0, and Nano Banana Pro inside Manus, with custom Skills ensuring agents prompt correctly.
items.author: higgsfield.ai

items.title: A free LLM API gateway pooling 11 providers with automatic failover
items.synopsis: The creator points to a trending repo offering a free LLM API that gives access to eleven free providers with over a billion tokens a month, including Gemini, DeepSeek, Kimi K and GLM among others. Its key feature is automatic failover: when one model runs out of tokens or hits a limit, requests move to the next provider automatically. He presents it as ideal for trying AI for the first time at no cost.
items.author: startscalr_sohum

items.title: Claude Automation Remembers All You Watch on Insta
items.synopsis: This French video demonstrates an automation that captures everything you watch on Instagram into a second brain powered by Claude. The idea is that saved reels and posts stop disappearing into the feed and become searchable knowledge. It is a personal-knowledge-management use case built on Claude automation.
items.author: 0xloucash

items.title: QMD: smarter file search for Claude
items.synopsis: The reel introduces QMD as a way to stop letting Claude search through your files on its own. QMD improves how Claude retrieves content from local files. Hashtags position it within the Claude, Codex, and Hermès agent ecosystem.
items.author: valentin_unmute

items.title: MiniCPM-V 4.6 runs on-device and beats models twice its size
items.synopsis: MiniCPM-V 4.6 comes out of Tsinghua University in Beijing and, unlike GPT-4o or Gemini which live in the cloud and require sending an image to a server, it runs on the device itself across iPhone, Android and Huawei's HarmonyOS. The trick is vision compression: since a model must first chop an image into tokens, cutting that vision encoding cost by 55% lets a 1.3-billion-parameter model do the work a 3-billion model used to. On benchmarks it beats larger models while using about 2.5% of the token budget, and it is Apache 2.0 licensed with free open weights.
items.author: v.i.s.h.ai

items.title: Claim: Claude killed n8n and OpenClaw
items.synopsis: The reel makes the provocative claim that Claude has made n8n and OpenClaw obsolete for building agents. Viewers comment 'Agents' to get a getting-started resource. The caption gives no detail on which Claude capability supposedly replaces those tools.
items.author: jeremyjcabral

items.title: Best AI tools for architecture and design
items.synopsis: The creator shares a curated list of the best AI tools and platforms for architecture and design work. Viewers comment 'OUTILS' to receive the list. The caption does not name the individual tools, only that the compilation is ready to share.
items.author: ad_render

items.title: Claude Code plugins that build an engineering team
items.synopsis: The reel argues most developers use Claude Code raw and are missing out. A set of plugins adds planning, UI design, code reviews, security scans, memory, and full dev workflows. With them, Claude Code feels less like an AI tool and more like an actual engineering team, with the full list shared via comment.
items.author: duncanrogoff

items.title: Why vlog-format AI influencers out-earn ones with 50x the following
items.synopsis: The creator contrasts AI influencers with barely 20,000 followers earning €50,000 a month against others with a million followers making under €10,000, and attributes the gap to format. Showcase videos of your AI influencer go viral and pull millions of views but attract only the curious, whereas vlogs create a parasocial bond in which the viewer feels they know the character and share her life — and that is what converts a follower into a customer. He says the vlog format quadrupled his own sales and offers a Claude AI agent that produces them correctly.
items.author: hugomatias.ai

items.title: Claude legal plugin: a 24/7 free law firm
items.synopsis: The reel promotes a new Claude plugin that acts like having a law firm at your fingertips, available 24/7 and completely free. The creator claims it can replace lawyers for everyday legal needs. An installation video is sent to viewers who comment 'LÉGAL'.
items.author: levibecodeur

items.title: Claude Taskmaster: turning a PRD into a full prioritised backlog in minutes
items.synopsis: Ugoia2025 presents Claude Taskmaster, an MCP server sitting around 27,000 GitHub stars, as the thing that quietly automated the project-scoping job. You hand Claude any document that describes a project — a spec, a PRD, a client brief — and the MCP generates the complete backlog from it: tickets, sub-tasks, inter-task dependencies and an automatic priority order. His own before-and-after is the pitch: three days of scoping meetings with his team replaced by roughly 80 ready tickets in four minutes.
items.author: ugoia2025

items.title: Printing Press : connecter les agents Claude Code à des sites sans API
items.synopsis: La skill GitHub CLI Printing Press s'installe en collant son URL directement dans le terminal Claude Code, et ouvre l'accès à des sites jusque-là fermés aux agents. On peut soit puiser dans la bibliothèque de printingpress.dev, qui couvre notamment Amazon, eBay, Shopify et TikTok, soit faire générer une CLI sur mesure pour un site précis : l'auteur l'a fait pour son application comptable dont il n'avait pas la clé API. Une fois la CLI en place il interroge ses vingt-cinq dernières factures depuis Claude Code, en consommant nettement moins de tokens qu'une connexion API ou qu'un serveur MCP.
items.author: bryanrichmaker

items.title: Claude + Stitch for production-ready UI systems
items.synopsis: The post tackles Claude's historical weakness at frontend work by pairing it with Stitch, Google's UI generation tool. The workflow uses Stitch to generate full UI systems and then turns them into production-ready apps with animations and connected screens. The full setup and prompts are gated behind a 'Code' comment.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Hermes Agent branché gratuitement sur Qwen 3.6 Plus et Owl Alpha
items.synopsis: Le post annonce une mise à jour gratuite d'Hermes Agent qui permet d'y connecter deux grands modèles sans frais, Qwen 3.6 Plus et Owl Alpha, crédités de mémoires plus larges que les modèles payants. Les usages promis sont la recherche de prospects, la rédaction d'e-mails et la recherche approfondie, en continu. La promesse de remplacer une équipe de recherche entière reste une affirmation commerciale non étayée.
items.author: aiexplained412

items.title: Le skill signé Boris Cherney qui couvre toutes les bonnes pratiques Claude Code
items.synopsis: Le post attribue au créateur de Claude Code, Boris Cherney, un skill présenté comme suffisant à lui seul. Il rassemblerait toutes les bonnes pratiques au même endroit : création d'agents, de commandes, de skills, de connexions, gestion de la mémoire, des paramètres, des workflows et de l'automatisation. L'auteur souligne qu'il procède de façon automatique en commençant par poser des questions sur le besoin, le lien étant envoyé par DM.
items.author: henriexploria

items.title: UI-TARS de ByteDance, alternative locale et gratuite à Manus
items.synopsis: UI-TARS est un outil de ByteDance positionné comme équivalent gratuit de Manus, facturé deux cents dollars par mois. On lui décrit une tâche et l'agent voit réellement l'écran, déplace la souris, clique et remplit les formulaires comme le ferait une personne assise devant l'ordinateur. Il fonctionne sans API ni code, s'exécute entièrement en local et reste donc privé, ce qui permet d'automatiser aussi bien la réservation d'un vol qu'un changement de réglages.
items.author: daniel.prompta

items.title: Quatre mises à jour Anthropic qui redéfinissent les agents
items.synopsis: L'auteur soutient que le changement décisif n'est venu ni d'un nouveau modèle ni d'une fonction de chatbot, mais de quatre évolutions discrètes. Elles permettent selon lui à une IA de recruter d'autres IA, d'évaluer son propre travail, de s'améliorer pendant la nuit et de rendre compte une fois la tâche terminée. Il présente cela comme le plus grand saut de capacité depuis l'arrivée des chatbots, sans nommer précisément les quatre fonctionnalités.
items.author: vaibhavsisinty

items.title: Hyperframer skill turns Claude into a motion design engine
items.synopsis: The reel demonstrates Hyperframer, a new skill developed by HeyGen that lets Claude generate advanced motion design. The creator claims it already buries existing tools like Remotion. All animations shown in the video were produced by Claude through this skill.
items.author: danyltn

items.title: WhatsApp Agent Kit lets Claude build a business chatbot with zero code
items.synopsis: The WhatsApp Agent Kit turns Claude into a builder for WhatsApp agents: you hand Claude the project link and it downloads the project and asks the right scoping questions — purpose, business name, desired tone. Once you answer, Claude constructs the agent, lets you test it directly in Claude, and configures deployment to WhatsApp, a web page, Telegram, or elsewhere. The creator pitches it for restaurants, clinics, online shops, and barbershops with no code required.
items.author: henriexploria

items.title: Un dépôt de bonnes pratiques qui structure tout un workflow Claude Code
items.synopsis: Le post présente un dépôt qui rassemble en un seul endroit prompts, skills, commandes et guides de configuration pour Claude Code, au lieu de les chercher au coup par coup. Les bénéfices annoncés sont un fonctionnement plus propre, une consommation de tokens réduite, une meilleure structure et un passage plus fluide de la planification à l'exécution. Le lien est envoyé par DM sur le mot-clé Skill.
items.author: startscalr_sohum

items.title: Le skill data.gouv ouvre 250 000 jeux de données publics français à Claude Code
items.synopsis: Le post décrit un skill qui permet d'interroger en langage naturel les données ouvertes de l'État français depuis Claude Code. Les exemples donnés sont concrets : connaître les entreprises du bâtiment créées à Lyon dans le mois via les données SIRENE en temps réel, ou obtenir un tableau filtré et analysé des permis de construire délivrés à Bordeaux en 2024. L'accès porte sur 250 000 jeux de données publics, gratuitement, le guide d'installation étant envoyé sur commentaire.
items.author: baptsimard.ia

items.title: Higgsfield, Claude Cowork et Meta assemblés en machine publicitaire autonome
items.synopsis: Montage en français décrivant un agent unique branché sur deux serveurs MCP pour faire tourner seule toute une chaîne de publicité Meta. Le cycle enchaîne recherche concurrentielle, génération de créas avec Sora 2, Veo et Kling, lancement des annonces sur Meta puis montée en charge sur les créas performantes. L'argument de vente est que l'ensemble s'exécute pendant que l'utilisateur dort, le guide complet passant par un commentaire.
items.author: pierrevibesai

items.title: ScrapeGraph-AI threatens paid scraping platforms
items.synopsis: A developer released ScrapeGraph-AI on GitHub, an open-source LLM-powered scraping tool that has already collected over 23,000 stars. The video claims it is replacing paid scraping platforms costing around 40,000 rupees a month. It frames the project as the moment free open-source AI killed the paid web-scraping market.
items.author: thevibefounder

items.title: Environ 80 modèles servis gratuitement par les API NVIDIA
items.synopsis: Le post signale l'accès gratuit à près de quatre-vingts modèles hébergés chez NVIDIA, dont MiniMax M2.7, GLM 5.1, Kimi 2.5, DeepSeek 3.2, GPT-OSS-120B et Sarvam-M. La configuration est détaillée noir sur blanc : récupérer une clé sur build.nvidia.com, pointer l'URL de base sur integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1, ajouter la clé et choisir le modèle. La compatibilité annoncée couvre OpenCode, Zed, Hermes Agent et Cursor.
items.author: thefutureguyy.ai

items.title: OpenCLI remplace Playwright MCP et divise la consommation de tokens
items.synopsis: Le post identifie un problème précis du pilotage de navigateur par Claude : la plupart des montages passent par Playwright MCP, qui renvoie une capture d'écran à chaque action — clic, formulaire, défilement — et sature le contexte en quelques minutes, pour environ dix fois trop de tokens. OpenCLI prend le contre-pied en transformant le site en outil en ligne de commande, registre que le modèle manipule bien plus efficacement que des images. L'auteur indique qu'il supporte nativement quatre-vingt-dix sites, dont Instagram, LinkedIn et Twitter, et s'installe en deux minutes.
items.author: dryxio.us

items.title: Des sites à effet parallaxe 3D générés depuis une simple vidéo
items.synopsis: Le post décrit une chaîne combinant Emergent et des skills Claude pour convertir des vidéos simples en animations de site à l'apparence tridimensionnelle. Le résultat est un site interactif à effet parallaxe, généré depuis des prompts puis personnalisable et publiable sans écrire de code. Le lien vers la méthode est conditionné à un commentaire.
items.author: nomadatoast

items.title: Une mémoire permanente pour Claude Code, en tête des tendances GitHub
items.synopsis: Le projet donne à Claude Code une mémoire permanente et a atteint la première place sur GitHub. L'argument central est la réduction de la consommation de tokens de 95%, ce qui repousse nettement le moment où l'on heurte les limites de débit. Le paquet inclut une recherche fondée sur les skills, une interface web de consultation et une skill supplémentaire pour utiliser Claude en desktop, le tout gratuit et installable en une seule commande, le lien partant en DM à qui commente Memory.
items.author: advicewithjean

items.title: Driving Claude Code with free open-source coding models
items.synopsis: The reel opens on a familiar wall — a Claude Code session that has run out of its usage allowance mid-project — and pitches a single configuration change that swaps the backend for open-weight coding models instead of paying for more. The caption frames it as running Qwen, Kimi or Gemma locally through Ollama and pointing Claude Code at that endpoint, while the Hindi voiceover claims the setup yielded roughly 15 million extra tokens at zero cost and names Kimi, Qwen3.5 and GLM as the models on offer. The actual configuration steps are withheld behind a "Comment CODE" DM gate, so the clip establishes the pattern — Claude Code as a client against a swappable model backend — without showing the wiring.
items.author: wdf_ai

items.title: Fix how Claude builds backlinks in Obsidian
items.synopsis: The reel argues most people use Obsidian with Claude wrong because they ignore the network of backlinks between notes. Backlinks turn isolated notes into a knowledge graph that AI can navigate and understand. The creator shows how to instruct Claude to create those connections, since it won't do so automatically.
items.author: sebastianhardy_

items.title: Kapso CLI donne un numéro WhatsApp à votre agent IA
items.synopsis: Le post présente Kapso CLI, un outil qui attribue un numéro WhatsApp à un agent IA et fait de la messagerie une plateforme d'exécution de workflows. Les cas listés sont le support client à deux heures du matin, les relances commerciales, les confirmations de commande et la prise de rendez-vous avec rappel, le tout depuis une seule conversation. L'argument de marché est que plus de deux milliards de personnes utilisent déjà WhatsApp quotidiennement.
items.author: thevibefounder

items.title: Google Workspace integrated with OpenClaw and Claude Code
items.synopsis: The post announces Google Workspace services being integrated with OpenClaw and Claude Code from the command line. The author reports this speeds up bringing services live, with over 100 skills being added to the setup. It is framed as a major win for teams running AI agents in production.
items.author: mattganzak

items.title: Top 5 jobs threatened by AI autonomous workforces
items.synopsis: The reel ranks the top five jobs the creator says are being destroyed right now by AI autonomous workforces. Hashtags place the discussion in the OpenClaw and vibe-coding ecosystem. It is commentary on labor disruption rather than a tool tutorial.
items.author: mattganzak

items.title: Cinq agents Microsoft Copilot qui font gagner du temps dès aujourd'hui
items.synopsis: Post en néerlandais qui part du constat que Microsoft Copilot reste flou à l'usage pour beaucoup d'utilisateurs. Il renvoie vers une vidéo gratuite présentant cinq agents Copilot applicables immédiatement dans le travail quotidien. Le contenu est un appât vers une ressource externe hébergée sur le site de l'auteur, sans détail des cas d'usage dans la légende.
items.author: flowkify

items.title: Voice Studio clones voices locally across 646 languages
items.synopsis: Voice Studio is an open-source voice-cloning and dubbing tool that has passed 35,000 GitHub stars and runs entirely on the user's own machine. From a short reference recording it clones a voice, then generates voice-overs, audiobooks or dubs any video into one of 646 languages, against roughly 70 for ElevenLabs. Because it runs locally there is no per-character billing and no audio leaves the machine, though the host warns to check each engine's commercial-use terms and to clone only your own voice.
items.author: simon_de_lima

items.title: xAI Voice Agents let AI place real phone calls
items.synopsis: xAI Voice Agents move AI agents from messaging into placing actual phone calls, configured by describing the desired behaviour in plain language. You choose the script and voice, get a phone number, and test before calling for real. A real-time speech-to-speech pipeline keeps latency low and can switch languages mid-conversation, targeting lead qualification and appointment booking.
items.author: thevibefounder

items.title: Fish Audio's S2.1 Pro takes aim at ElevenLabs, free via API until 31 August
items.synopsis: The creator claims Fish Audio's newly released S2.1 Pro model is undercutting ElevenLabs, the world leader in AI voice, by being completely free for developers through the API until 31 August. It generates voices, clones your own in about fifteen seconds, and can produce entirely new ones at a price he says defies competition. His kicker is that everything you hear in the video was built end to end by Claude Code without ever opening the website, using a custom skill he wrote and offers to send.
items.author: thomasbssh

items.title: Run a voice-cloning research model locally
items.synopsis: A voice AI project has brought a powerful research model onto consumer machines. It supports cloning voices locally and experimenting with AI conversations without a cloud subscription. The creator frames it as open-source voice technology for people who want to explore without recurring costs.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Voicebox clones a voice locally from three seconds of audio
items.synopsis: Voicebox is an open-source voice studio that runs entirely on your own machine — no cloud, no account, no subscription — and the creator narrates the whole video with a clone of his own voice produced by typing text. Three seconds of audio suffice to clone a voice, screen audio can be captured to clone from a video, and seven engines are available (he used Qwen 1.7B), tested deliberately against hard technical vocabulary like MCP, n8n, and long token counts. He closes on an ethical note about the homepage offering Morgan Freeman, Obama, and Scarlett Johansson voices — cloning your own voice is a choice, cloning someone else's without asking is another matter.
items.author: dupflodev

items.title: Voicebox 0.50: a local-first voice studio with full MCP integration
items.synopsis: Closing a weekly GitHub roundup, the creator covers Voicebox at 34,000 stars — up 3,700 that week — released by Jamie Pine, the developer behind Spacedrive, as a complete local-first AI voice studio. It clones any voice from only three seconds of audio, generates speech in 23 languages across seven TTS engines including Alibaba's Qwen3 TTS, and offers a global keyboard shortcut for dictation in any application. The part he flags as genuinely interesting for developers is full MCP integration, meaning a Claude Code or Cursor agent can speak with your cloned voice via Model Context Protocol, all running locally so no audio data leaves the machine — an MIT open-source alternative to ElevenLabs and Wispr Flow.
items.author: sebastien_heilig

items.title: Qwen 3 TTS Clones Your Voice From 3 Seconds
items.synopsis: This French video pitches Qwen 3 as the best open-source text-to-speech model available, a free ElevenLabs replacement. It clones a voice from just three seconds of audio and generates unlimited dialogue. You can describe the voice you want and adjust tone, rhythm, and style.
items.author: arthurjanicaud

items.title: AI week: 3-second voice cloning and Claude in Excel
items.synopsis: This rapid-fire weekly AI recap leads with a free Chinese voice model that clones any voice in 3 seconds, alongside a new real-time image editing tool. The countdown also covers Anthropic launching Claude in Excel, which analyzes multi-tab workbooks and debugs formulas. The format packs the week's AI headlines into under 60 seconds.
items.author: drcintas

items.title: ImagineArt Lipsync Studio with Nano Banana Pro characters
items.synopsis: The creator tests ImagineArt's new Lipsync Studio, which lip-syncs any character using a photo plus an audio sample of your voice or plain text. Combined with ImagineArt's Nano Banana Pro image model, the same character can be reused consistently across generations. It is a hands-on demo of a photo-to-talking-character pipeline.
items.author: ashokreddyai

items.title: Fadr auto-matches tempo and key for instant mashups
items.synopsis: Fadr promotes its remixing platform that lets users mash up favorite songs without knowing BPM or musical keys. Tempo and key are matched automatically so mashups sound right out of the box. The post pushes a holiday deal pricing Fadr+ at 50 dollars per year until December 1, 2025.
items.author: fadrmusic

items.title: A no-login site that clones any voice from ten seconds of audio
items.synopsis: Presented as part of a running 'tools you probably shouldn't know' series and framed as educational only, the site clones anyone's voice with no login required. You upload or record at least ten seconds of speech — more audio yields a more accurate clone — and must type out exactly what was recorded so the AI has correct reference text. The creator then plays a clone of his own voice saying arbitrary text and remarks on how unsettling the capability has become.
items.author: ariacodez

items.title: Video cloning tools compared: Runway and WAN 2.2
items.synopsis: This French post lists the tools needed to clone a video, starting with Runway, which offers a free trial and a roughly 15-euro monthly subscription discounted with the code MADSAL. The second option is WAN 2.2, with the caveat that the WAN app is not free. It is a practical mini tool guide rather than a single-product promo.
items.author: ninon.ia_officiel

items.title: Text-to-sound-effects AI generates 30 seconds of loopable Hollywood audio
items.synopsis: The tool turns a plain prompt such as 'soft rain' into up to thirty seconds of crystal-clear, seamlessly looping audio. The creator reports testing it for games, video backing tracks, and ambient background use, with consistently smooth and accurate results. It is pitched as a way to get Hollywood-grade sound effects into a video effortlessly.
items.author: theaisurfer

items.title: MiniMax Speech 02 HD clones a voice from ten seconds, free
items.synopsis: The reel presents MiniMax Speech 02 HD as a Chinese voice model topping global benchmarks and beating OpenAI and ElevenLabs. Ten seconds of audio is enough to clone a voice, and the model supports 30-plus languages, emotion control, and very long inputs. The free tier gives 5,000 characters per day plus one voice clone to try it out.
items.author: v.i.s.h.ai

items.title: Cloning a stranger's voice from a 30-second YouTube clip
items.synopsis: The creator demonstrates voice cloning end to end by taking a 30-second clip from YouTube, saving the audio, and uploading it to a voice-cloning site under a new clone name. After a short wait the clone is ready and he plays back generated speech in the target's voice to confirm it works. He closes by calling it very powerful and urging viewers to use it for good.
items.author: winkguys

items.title: SpeechMA and two more free ElevenLabs alternatives
items.synopsis: The post argues you no longer need to pay for ElevenLabs and lists three free AI voice generators of comparable quality. The first named is SpeechMA, offering over 400 voices across 60 languages with no signup and unlimited use. The full trio is delivered via DM to viewers commenting VOICE.
items.author: nick_saraev

items.title: Creator fully cloned by trained voice and image models
items.synopsis: The creator presents a video generated entirely by AI using models trained on his own voice and image. He reflects on how far generative AI has come in such a short time and what this means for our notion of authentic content. The post is an early, thoughtful self-cloning demonstration rather than a tool promotion.
items.author: jaschasuess

items.title: An AI that turns any topic into a personalised audio lesson in your inbox
items.synopsis: The creator pitches learning anything in minutes, Matrix-style: you type what you want to learn and how much time you want to spend on it, and the tool emails you an audio file covering the subject. The idea is to convert the ten or fifteen minutes spent commuting or scrolling into study time by simply putting headphones on. He states the tool is free and sends the link to commenters.
items.author: antony_nonis

items.title: Evo, an AI that wrote working viral genomes from scratch
items.synopsis: Researchers showed the Evo model more than two million bacteriophage genomes — viruses that attack and destroy bacteria — and it learned, recombined, and began inventing entirely new genetic sequences never seen in nature. Many were tested in the laboratory and sixteen of them actually worked, infecting and eliminating E. coli strains, with some more effective than their natural equivalents. The clip frames this as the first time an AI has written living genomes, a historic breakthrough that is also unnerving because an AI able to create life might one day destroy it.
items.author: supernova.hablo

items.title: Website-cloning tool driven by twelve abliterated agents is released free
items.synopsis: The author announces that a previously paid tool has been made free, giving anyone access to an abliterated, guardrail-stripped model stack described as the unrestricted equivalent of ChatGPT and Claude. You supply a URL and an array of twelve abliterated AI agents reconstructs the site or software behind it, the pitch being that you no longer settle for a generic AI-built landing page when you can rebuild one you already like. Because an exact copy is not supplied, the tool regenerates the visuals and branding to the user's own specification, which is framed as making any digital asset yours and is plainly an intellectual-property grey zone worth flagging.
items.author: realrobertgutierrez

items.title: NVIDIA PAIR spreads local inference across your own machines
items.synopsis: Matthew Berman covers NVIDIA PAIR, the Personal AI Router, which lets you run local AI from one computer while other compatible machines on the network service the requests. A second desktop, an older gaming PC or a supported Apple device can contribute spare compute, and PAIR measures what is available on each device and routes accordingly. If you start gaming on one machine it shifts work elsewhere, each machine handling its own inference, and the tool is free; the post is sponsored by NVIDIA.
items.author: matthewberman_ai

items.title: Stacking prompt fragments instead of firing single AI “codes”
items.synopsis: A carousel arguing that one-shot prompt snippets underperform because they give a generative model only a single axis of direction. The proposed fix is a six-slot stack — niche, goal, style, details, platform, output — assembled into one composite instruction so the model receives the full brief at once. The post shows the slot structure itself but keeps the worked examples behind a follow-and-save call to action.
items.author: richmeetings.ai

items.title: Criteria for being featured as an AI-built business
items.synopsis: The account lists what a business must satisfy to be featured: being a real, active product or service already launched or operating, and being a small or growing brand with no requirement for size or following. The business must genuinely use AI in a meaningful role in building, growing or running itself, and be able to tell that story concretely. It must also be willing to share process, tools, workflows, examples or outcomes, and have a public presence such as Instagram or a website.
items.author: richmeetings.ai

items.title: 20 prompt recipes turning clothing photos into fashion campaign shots
items.synopsis: A carousel of twenty prompt recipes aimed at apparel sellers, converting flat product photography into model shoots, lookbooks, seasonal collections, bridal campaigns and in-store displays. The pitch is that a brand can generate campaign-grade imagery from garment photos it already owns rather than commissioning a shoot. The carousel frames each use case but routes the detailed prompt text to the creator channel.
items.author: richmeetings.ai

items.title: Eight prompts that split brand building into distinct AI roles
items.synopsis: The carousel contrasts traditional brand building, weeks of strategy calls, design revisions and website development costing thousands, with what a founder can now compress using Claude. The claimed output path runs from a rough business idea through brand positioning, messaging, visual direction, website structure, launch copy and an iteration plan.
