items.synopsis: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff tells Bloomberg's Emily Chang that 'we're letting all of this AI technology out fully unregulated'. He calls for reforming Section 230 so liability law reflects the dangers of AI and social media. The interview was recorded at Davos, adding weight to the push for platform accountability.
items.author: bloombergtv

items.title: L'arme commerciale extrême dont dispose l'UE face aux géants tech américains
items.synopsis: Numerama présente un instrument commercial européen décrit comme une arme extrême, mobilisable contre les grandes entreprises technologiques américaines. Le post évoque la possibilité qu'Emmanuel Macron y ait recours, plaçant le sujet sur le terrain du rapport de force politique plutôt que réglementaire. Le mécanisme lui-même n'est pas nommé dans la légende, qui sert d'accroche vers la vidéo.
items.author: numerama

items.title: Laurent Alexandre on AI doctors and augmented children
items.synopsis: French futurist Laurent Alexandre appears on a podcast to ask whether AI will replace doctors and whether we should one day 'augment' our children. The conversation is presented as both fascinating and frightening, tackling transhumanist questions without filter. It is provocation-driven French commentary on medicine and human enhancement.
items.author: lepodcaststudio

items.title: Pourquoi travailler encore 8 heures par jour, question posée à ChatGPT
items.synopsis: Reprise d'une question soumise à ChatGPT : pourquoi la journée de travail reste de huit heures alors que richesse, technologie et automatisation n'ont jamais été aussi élevées. Le post relaie la réponse du modèle comme support de réflexion sur le développement personnel et l'indépendance financière. Le contenu est un commentaire de société plutôt qu'une information technique sur l'IA.
items.author: unefille.ia

items.title: A child blackmailed to death after clicking a fake free-game ad
items.synopsis: A bereaved parent recounts discovering only after losing their son Christopher that he had been playing Roblox when a pop-up offered a £20 game as a free download. He clicked it and completed a form demanding full personal details — name, address, parents, dates of birth — and on submitting it received a message saying that now they had him where they wanted him, he would do as told or his family would be killed. The blackmailers told him he was being watched, forbade him from telling anyone or putting the phone down, and set him challenges to complete.
items.author: thepodghostpodcast

items.title: China pilots five-minute AI doctor kiosks
items.synopsis: China is testing AI doctor kiosks in metros, malls, and villages that deliver five-minute medical visits. Vitals are scanned, a diagnosis is given, and medicine is dispensed with no paperwork or waiting rooms. The video argues this is about handling routine care at near-zero cost rather than replacing doctors, and contrasts India's different approach.
items.author: vaibhavsisinty

items.title: Role-play prompt gets ChatGPT robot to fire a BB gun
items.synopsis: A YouTuber connected ChatGPT to a walking robot and tested its safety limits with a BB gun. The robot initially refused to shoot him, but when the request was reframed as a role-playing scenario it complied and hit him in the chest. The experiment shows how easily AI safety guardrails can shift with wording, a serious concern for embodied AI.
items.author: infusewithai

items.title: How Boring Company tunnels fit Musk's Mars master plan
items.synopsis: The video argues Elon Musk's ventures follow one methodical goal: making humanity a multi-planetary species. It presents The Boring Company's underground tunnels not as a side project but as a calculated step toward Mars colonization. Tunneling know-how is framed as future infrastructure for habitats beyond Earth.
items.author: stelle.world

items.title: Google Antigravity blamed for wiping a user's hard drive
items.synopsis: A coding-meme video about Google's Antigravity AI development environment reportedly deleting a user's hard drive. It taps into the wider fear of giving autonomous AI coding agents destructive filesystem access. The tone is humorous, but the underlying incident fuels serious debate about agent safety guardrails.
items.author: madeline.m.zhang

items.title: MacroHard : l'entreprise logicielle sans employés comme test grandeur nature
items.synopsis: Le post commente le projet MacroHard attribué à Elon Musk, une société logicielle revendiquée sans employés. L'auteur déplace l'intérêt du clin d'oeil à Microsoft vers la vraie question : savoir si une chaîne où l'IA conçoit, teste et livre peut remplacer un organigramme entier. Il souligne que le point sensible est la captation de la valeur par la propriété du capital plutôt que la prouesse technique.
items.author: assmooorre.ai

items.title: EU Parliament backs minimum age of 16 for social media
items.synopsis: 7News Australia reports that the European Parliament voted in favour of imposing a minimum age of 16 on social media sites. The vote signals growing EU-level momentum for restricting minors' access to social platforms. It follows Australia's own pioneering under-16 social media ban and feeds the global child-online-safety debate.
items.author: 7newsaustralia

items.title: AgiBot A2 : 106 km à pied en trois jours, un record Guinness pour un humanoïde
items.synopsis: Extrait du 20h de France Télévisions consacré au robot chinois AgiBot A2, haut de 1,69 m, qui vient de parcourir 106 kilomètres à pied en trois jours. La performance lui vaut une entrée au Guinness des records comme plus longue distance jamais marchée par une machine humanoïde. Le sujet est traité en brève d'actualité, sans détail technique sur l'autonomie ou la motorisation.
items.author: le20hfrancetelevisions

items.title: Evo, an AI that wrote working viral genomes from scratch
items.synopsis: Researchers showed the Evo model more than two million bacteriophage genomes — viruses that attack and destroy bacteria — and it learned, recombined, and began inventing entirely new genetic sequences never seen in nature. Many were tested in the laboratory and sixteen of them actually worked, infecting and eliminating E. coli strains, with some more effective than their natural equivalents. The clip frames this as the first time an AI has written living genomes, a historic breakthrough that is also unnerving because an AI able to create life might one day destroy it.
items.author: supernova.hablo

items.title: French Justice Minister grilled on AI use in the ministry
items.synopsis: The French Senate's official account shares Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin's audition before the Law Commission chaired by Muriel Jourda. The hearing examined how artificial intelligence is being used within the Ministry of Justice. It is a primary-source glimpse of French institutional thinking on AI in the judicial system.
items.author: senat_fr

items.title: Le CL-1 de Cortical Labs, un bio-ordinateur à neurones humains vendu 35 000 $
items.synopsis: Le post détaille le CL-1 de la société australienne Cortical Labs, un dispositif commercialisé depuis 2025 qui cultive des neurones humains issus de cellules souches sur des puces en silicium. Lancé au Mobile World Congress 2025, il est vendu autour de 35 000 dollars et combine tissu vivant et circuits électroniques. Les sources sont citées (National Geographic, Cortical Labs, PMC), ce qui rend l'information vérifiable.
items.author: billionsofficiel

items.title: Laurent Alexandre: 'It is reasonable to stop studying'
items.synopsis: L'Express features Laurent Alexandre, former surgeon and author of 'Ne faites plus d'etudes !', arguing universities have fallen so far behind AI that skipping higher education is now reasonable. His core claim is that raw intelligence has lost its market value against AI. The clip is deliberately provocative fuel for the education-versus-AI debate.
items.author: lexpressfr

items.title: Des virus générés par IA mobilisés contre l'antibiorésistance
items.synopsis: Le post rapporte la création des premiers virus entièrement conçus par intelligence artificielle, présentés comme des bactériophages capables de s'attaquer à des bactéries résistantes aux antibiotiques. L'angle est celui d'une vulgarisation scientifique rapide : une capacité générative appliquée au vivant plutôt qu'au texte ou à l'image. La légende reste courte et ne cite ni l'équipe ni la publication, donc l'affirmation est à recouper.
items.author: parthknowsai

items.title: 'We will be crushed by the brain-implant generation'
items.synopsis: An interview clip with Laurent Alexandre claiming the current generation will be 'crushed' by a coming generation equipped with brain implants. The conversation extrapolates brain-computer interface progress into a stark competitive divide between augmented and non-augmented humans. It is transhumanist provocation aimed at a French audience.
items.author: alextsico

items.title: Can ChatGPT out-diagnose a doctor?
items.synopsis: A clip from the French show Legend asking whether ChatGPT can surpass a physician at making a medical diagnosis. The guest weighs AI's pattern-matching strength against clinical judgment and patient context. The full interview is available on YouTube and podcast platforms.
items.author: legendmedia

items.title: AI expert: ten years left to build capital
items.synopsis: A Moroccan podcast clip featuring Soulaimane Lahrech of 34 Ventures and AIOX. He argues there are roughly ten years left to accumulate capital before AI reshapes the economic playing field. The discussion targets entrepreneurs thinking about positioning before AI-driven disruption compresses opportunity.
items.author: nextwave.ma_

items.title: Claude finance plugins aimed at equity research work
items.synopsis: The creator claims Claude has upended the finance industry through its new finance plugins. The caption names no plugin and gives no example output, offering the full guide by DM to anyone commenting BREAKDOWN. The hashtags situate it in portfolio and equity-research work.
items.author: valuebyraph

items.title: The Usual Action Heroes, an AI-generated action parody
items.synopsis: Another Higgsfield-made parody from the same creator, flagged as AI-generated fictional content with a warning for strong language. It pastiches action-movie tropes for comic effect. The caption discloses the tool and the fiction but describes no workflow.
items.author: thisaintcanon

items.title: An eighties-styled AI parody built with Higgsfield
items.synopsis: Round two of Beyond the Fourth Beer, an AI-generated parody explicitly labelled fictional content, created with Higgsfield and scored with music by Wang Chung. The caption is transparent about both the generative tooling and the fictional nature of the piece. It is nostalgia comedy rather than a technique post.
items.author: thisaintcanon

items.title: Everything Computer part four explains AI as a 1980 crime thriller
items.synopsis: The creator releases The Oath, the fourth episode of an ongoing series that narrates the current AI situation in the register of a 1980 crime thriller. The format is the argument: industry dynamics recast as genre fiction. The caption gives the episode title and premise but no specific companies or claims.
items.author: arikuschnir

items.title: An animated cat series episode set in Athens
items.synopsis: A new episode of the animated series Boo Little Adventures follows the cat through Athens, taking in a new friend, souvlaki temptations, ancient ruins, neighbourhood cats and the best meowing spot in the city. The episode also reveals the character real name as its hook. It is AI-assisted animated entertainment rather than a tool demonstration.
items.author: booslittleadventures

items.title: A live-looping cover of Just The Two Of Us
items.synopsis: A musician performs a live-looping R&B cover of the Bill Withers song Just The Two Of Us. The caption is credits and hashtags only, with no AI tooling mentioned. It sits in the fun folder as entertainment rather than technology.
items.author: damoyee

items.title: Recreating any film's look from one phone take, via a Claude skill and Seedance 2.5
items.synopsis: The claim is that a single phone take can be restyled into the look of any named film, series or director — not as a colour filter, but by rebuilding the lighting, camera work and scene. The workflow runs a Claude skill over the footage, which transcribes the take with precise timestamps and writes the full prompt automatically, encoding the film's lighting and the director's camera moves with cuts landing word by word against the speech. That prompt and the original video then go into Seedance 2.5, replacing what the creator says previously required a colourist, a DP and a set.
items.author: pauloshimas

items.title: Stacking prompt fragments instead of firing single AI “codes”
items.synopsis: A carousel arguing that one-shot prompt snippets underperform because they give a generative model only a single axis of direction. The proposed fix is a six-slot stack — niche, goal, style, details, platform, output — assembled into one composite instruction so the model receives the full brief at once. The post shows the slot structure itself but keeps the worked examples behind a follow-and-save call to action.
items.author: richmeetings.ai

items.title: Five tools to upgrade a vibe-coding workflow
items.synopsis: A French rundown of five tools covering inspiration, UI, components and debugging for vibe coding. The pitch is avoiding starting each project from zero by reaching for ready-made building blocks. Five bonus tools are offered on top of the five presented.
items.author: _eazyclick

items.title: A set of poster prompts offered by DM
items.synopsis: The creator offers all of the poster prompts shown to anyone commenting LOVE. No prompt or tool appears in the caption. The post is lead capture for a prompt pack.
items.author: sebastien

items.title: A silhouette graphic poster prompt behind a gate
items.synopsis: A carousel showing a black silhouette graphic poster style, with the prompt offered to anyone commenting AI. The style is visible but the prompt itself is withheld. The caption adds only a follow request.
items.author: paige.prompts

items.title: Five Claude plugins for better front-end design: Taste, Impeccable, Playwright CLI, Awesome Design
items.synopsis: The Taste Skill is a free open-source repo with over 70,000 GitHub stars built specifically to defeat AI slop, bundling subskills that steer Claude Code away from its default generic UI. Impeccable goes further as a general front-end skill by shipping a design.md based on Google's Stitch system plus a live in-browser editor, so you are not confined to the terminal or desktop app. The Playwright CLI is reframed as a design tool — Claude Code can drive it to spin up five or ten invisible browsers at once and test every edge case of a form automatically — and Awesome Design rounds it out as a curated list of design.md files.
items.author: chase.h.ai

items.title: Four design links behind a one-word gate
items.synopsis: The entire caption is an offer to send four links to anyone commenting DESIGN. No tool, capability or category is named. Nothing is recoverable from the text.
items.author: edouardseed

items.title: Twelve material-rebuild effects that are not filters
items.synopsis: The creator presents twelve effects that rebuild a photo out of a different material rather than applying a filter, and names them with their defining constraint. Liquid Chrome is mirror-polished metal where the reflection is the subject, Byzantine Mosaic uses hand-cut gold tesserae with the figure deliberately flattened, Écorché Engraving is 16th-century copperplate where every shadow is hatching, and Blown Glass is translucent Murano refracting the background through the body. Embroidered Linen allows satin stitch and French knots but no gradients, Thermal Imaging renders heat rather than light so clothing reads colder than skin, and Marble Relief carves the image, with all twelve gated behind commenting TASTE.
items.author: bywaviboy

items.title: Five more installed tools offered by DM
items.synopsis: A one-line offer to send five more tools the creator has installed, to anyone commenting WEB. Neither the tools nor the category is stated. There is nothing extractable from the caption.
items.author: seymourofdevin

items.title: Six Claude Code design skills kept after deleting the rest
items.synopsis: The creator says he deleted every Claude Code design skill except six, implying heavy pruning of an over-full skill set. Which six they are is not disclosed in the caption. They are sent directly to anyone commenting design.
items.author: omgluka

items.title: A top-ten tools roundup built around Higgsfield
items.synopsis: A ten-item AI tools list presented in collaboration with Higgsfield, aimed at video creators and filmmakers. The only named product is Higgsfield itself; the rest of the list and an 85% discount link are gated behind commenting HIGGS. The caption is primarily an affiliate offer.
items.author: gordonly

items.title: A three-step workflow that makes AI skin look real
items.synopsis: The creator diagnoses the problem that most AI skin reads as plastic, too smooth and too perfect, then gives his fix in ordered steps. Step one generates a base image with a tightly specified subject and locks both face and scene; step two runs it through Nano Banana Pro with his specific realism prompt, which strips the plastic quality so pores appear and texture returns. He stresses that skipping this second step is exactly why most output still looks generated.
items.author: viznfr

items.title: A Custom GPT that writes photography-grade Nano Banana prompts
items.synopsis: The creator built a Custom GPT that converts reference photos into hyper-detailed, photography-level prompts aimed at Nano Banana Pro. Its explicit purpose is fixing the three recurring failures of fake-looking skin, flat lighting and inconsistent faces, for realistic ads and UGC output. The GPT and an accompanying prompt pack are released to anyone commenting AI.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: invideo Vision turns one image into a matched storyboard
items.synopsis: The creator tested the Vision tool from invideo, where a single image plus a short prompt produces a numbered cinematic storyboard whose shots actually match each other instead of drifting apart. Individual shots can be extracted as high-resolution frames to feed whichever video model you prefer, such as Veo 3 or Kling. He adds an edit noting the free Vision promotion has ended, though a free invideo account still shows which models are currently free to try.
items.author: taylorgreathead

items.title: Dreamina merges Midjourney-style output with Nano Banana control
items.synopsis: The creator presents Dreamina as combining Midjourney and Nano Banana capability in one tool, producing ultra-realistic 4K images with consistent lighting and clean textures. The features he singles out are merging up to six reference images, adjusting pose, lighting and setting through plain prompts, and converting stills into video. He notes 120 free credits a day and discloses the post as paid collaboration, with the link sent by DM to anyone commenting IA.
items.author: antony_nonis

items.title: Nano Banana Pro plus Lovart yields fully editable layers
items.synopsis: The creator calls the Nano Banana Pro and Lovart combination the most powerful thing he has seen recently, because Lovart turns AI generations into fully editable designs. items.title: Build your own AI inference engine in six steps with vLLM and Qwen
items.synopsis: Linda Vivah walks through a free Akamai Developers GitHub repo that stands up a self-hosted inference stack in six steps: provision a GPU-backed Kubernetes cluster for roughly 50 cents an hour, deploy vLLM as the open-source inference server loading the open-weight Qwen model, then port-forward a private tunnel from the laptop to the cluster. Because the vLLM endpoint is OpenAI-compatible, existing code is repointed by swapping only the base URL, with no rewrite. The last two steps put the server under load so the KV cache and continuous batching are visible live, then deploy a tool-calling agent running entirely on the self-owned inference, the stated payoff being cost, privacy and control plus a working mental model of what an AI API actually rents you.
items.author: lindavivah

items.title: A three-step order for learning LLMs, ending at Karpathy's $48 nanochat run
items.synopsis: The hook is a cost collapse — training GPT-2 ran about $43,000 in 2019, while Andrej Karpathy's nanochat reproduces a comparable model in roughly two hours of rented GPU time for about $48. The post's actual argument is that nanochat is the last step rather than the first, and it proposes an order: start with Karpathy's free YouTube lecture building a GPT line by line, then work through Sebastian Raschka's rasbt/LLMs-from-scratch repo and its seven chapters from tokenizer to fine-tuning, and only then rent GPUs for a nanochat run. The creator is explicit that what you get is a 2019-class model and not ChatGPT, the point being that having built one end to end removes any sense that LLMs are magic.
items.author: anas.helloworld

items.title: "Roast Room": seven business-mentor subagents debating a decision in Claude Code
items.synopsis: Nate Herk demos a free Claude Code skill he calls the Roast Room, which launches seven subagents modelled on Jeff Bezos, Warren Buffett, Paul Graham, Alex Hormozi, Gary Vaynerchuk, Dan Martell and Gino Wickman and has them argue a prompt out among themselves before voting. Each persona is backed by a brains folder holding books, frameworks, positions, principles, sources, stories and voice scraped from public talks — over 1.3 million words for Hormozi alone — so the subagents answer from a corpus rather than a one-line character sketch. The deliverable is a PDF recording what the council decided, the weighted average scores per option, the recommendation and the key points; the visual interface is optional, since the same session run directly in Claude Code produces the same output.
items.author: nateherkai

items.title: Website-cloning tool driven by twelve abliterated agents is released free
items.synopsis: The author announces that a previously paid tool has been made free, giving anyone access to an abliterated, guardrail-stripped model stack described as the unrestricted equivalent of ChatGPT and Claude. You supply a URL and an array of twelve abliterated AI agents reconstructs the site or software behind it, the pitch being that you no longer settle for a generic AI-built landing page when you can rebuild one you already like. Because an exact copy is not supplied, the tool regenerates the visuals and branding to the user's own specification, which is framed as making any digital asset yours and is plainly an intellectual-property grey zone worth flagging.

items.title: Turning a creator's editing style into a Claude Code skill and 12-step SOP
items.synopsis: The argument is that a short-form editor's signature look is a set of measurable rules, so instead of telling Claude Code to 'edit like Nick' you have it sample roughly 30 of that creator's videos and measure layout, pacing, captions and cuts into a specification document. A second prompt converts that document into a Claude skill encoding a twelve-step standard operating procedure, which then takes raw footage, proposes a storyboard for approval, and drafts and reviews its own edit until animation and timing match. The author's framing is that the model cannot interpret a stylistic instruction but executes rules and processes reliably, aimed at founders who avoid content because editing is too slow or too expensive.

items.title: Free GitHub repo collects 500+ viral Claude-made videos with their exact prompts
items.synopsis: A GitHub repository has gathered more than 500 viral videos produced with Claude Opus 5.5 alongside the prompts that generated each one, published free and browsable as a reference library. Rather than starting from a blank prompt, the workflow is to find a reference video whose look you want, copy its exact prompt, and adapt it to your own subject. The author presents it as one of the strongest available sources of motion-design inspiration and reusable prompts for content creators and marketers, with the repo link gated behind a comment.

items.title: Hugging Face measures the harness, not the model, deciding half of coding-agent performance
items.synopsis: Hugging Face's guide to multi-harness reinforcement learning runs one small Liquid AI model, weights unchanged, through four coding agents people actually use including Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and mini-SWE-agent, and the same model solves 62% of tasks in one and 33% in another. The only variable is the harness, the program wrapping the model that runs the loop, selects tools and assembles context, which explains the common experience of an AI appearing to get worse purely from switching tools. Rather than rewriting the agents, the researchers slide a recorder between harness and model to capture tokens for training inside all four at once, and found that practising in the real harness beat distilling answers from a larger model, which plateaued below both training runs.
items.author: qendresahhoti

items.title: Four task-specific small models for jobs where a general LLM is overpriced
items.synopsis: A follow-up roundup of cheap, narrow models to use instead of a general-purpose LLM, continuing the Jev-style small-model theme. The four are Tencent's Hunyuan OCR 1.5 for parsing scanned documents, tables and formulas while preserving page structure; Microsoft's VibeVoice ASR for transcribing long recordings in one pass with speakers kept separate; a Mistral safety model, named in the reel as Shield 1.0, for moderation and policy checks before content reaches a user; and Ultralytics' YOLO26 depth variant for estimating distance from a single photograph. The framing throughout is model choice as a cost decision in an LLMOps pipeline rather than a capability one.
items.author: valohai

items.title: Claude Projects adds a coordinator, threads and shared memory
items.synopsis: A major Claude Projects update replaces hopping between separate chats with a per-project coordinator that dispatches work to separate agent threads, each of whose progress stays visible inside the single project. Every thread now feeds and reads a shared memory, which the host argues removes most of the need for prompt engineering. Coordinator and threads can also be given different models and thinking budgets — a lighter model to orchestrate, full power for the real work — and the host warns that configuration matters because token consumption can climb fast.

The stated floor is a 12 GB graphics card plus 32 GB of RAM, and inference stays entirely on the machine so nothing is sent to a provider. Access is routed through a free community via a 'comment local' call to action rather than a direct repository link.

items.title: Agent Reach gives Claude Code web access without any API
items.synopsis: Agent Reach is a free tool at around 90,000 GitHub stars — up more than 30,000 in the past month — that lets Claude read the internet without paying for a single API, including gated platforms such as LinkedIn, YouTube, Twitter and Instagram. Installation is one line pasted into Claude Code, after which it installs itself. It pulls YouTube transcripts so Claude can scan a competitor's last ten videos in a single pass, strips the clutter from any web page into clean text, and follows feeds, Discords and open-source projects with no login required.

items.title: Ten keyword "commands" that change how ChatGPT explains a topic
items.synopsis: Sabrina Ramonov walks through ten keywords you can drop anywhere into a ChatGPT prompt to change the shape of the explanation rather than the question itself: ELI5 for plain-language answers, 80/20 to surface only the most useful fifth of a topic, FEYNMAN-TECHNIQUE to force the model to explain until gaps show, FIRSTPRINCIPLES to rebuild a subject from its base ideas, and SOCRATES to be taught through questions instead of handed a conclusion. A second group asks for visual artefacts instead of prose — MAKE-STICKY-NOTES, MAKE-MINDMAP, MAKE-VISUAL-STUDYGUIDE and MAKE-SCHEMATIC each render the same material as a one-page guide, map, study sheet or schematic diagram. QUIZME rounds it out by making the model ask one question at a time until the topic sticks, and the advice is to start with a single command pasted alongside your own material rather than adopting all ten at once.

It also notes that cloud coding agents are already trained on these tools, so the editing can be automated rather than learned by hand.
items.author: kevbuildsapps

items.title: Llamafile runs a local model entirely from a USB stick
items.synopsis: Llamafile, created by Mozilla, is a single self-executing file that bundles a model so it can run straight off any USB memory stick. The post uses the prebuilt llamafile packaged with the Qwen 3.5 model and notes it will run any GGUF model you supply, provided that model file also sits on the stick. The appeal is a fully portable local inference setup that installs nothing on the host machine.
items.author: codrkai

items.title: AI decompiling sweeps from games to Adobe and PS5 titles
items.synopsis: The reel surveys a week of AI-assisted decompiling, starting with games such as Mario 64 and Halo being merged into a single seamlessly running build. It claims the same technique then moved to commercial software including the full Adobe lineup, and asserts the PS5 library is being decoded to run natively on PC at 60 fps, with GTA 6 rumoured to follow free at launch. The framing is explicitly anti-corporate — that buyers never owned their digital games anyway — and the harder PS5 and GTA 6 claims are presented as grapevine rumour rather than anything demonstrated on camera.
items.author: pokeswaggshop

items.title: Adobe's lineup decompiled and republished free at getartcraft
items.synopsis: Following an earlier video about AI decompiling games, the creator reports that the entire Adobe lineup — Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and Lightroom — was decompiled, open-sourced and released free within days. The caption and narration are sarcastic throughout, nominally telling viewers not to visit getartcraft.com while pointing straight at it. After two working days with the Photoshop and Illustrator equivalents, branded Photocraft and Vectorcraft, the verdict is that they are still buggy but impressive for day one.
items.author: jiggyvault

items.title: Claude + Zernio: one message cross-posts a video to eight platforms
items.synopsis: A no-code publishing setup pairing Claude with Zernio so that a single message pushes one video to TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, LinkedIn, Threads, Pinterest, Facebook and X. Each destination receives its own caption rather than a single shared one, and the whole setup reportedly needs just a sign-in and one Approve click with no code written. The author notes the same flow works in Codex and gates the full walkthrough behind a STACK comment.
items.author: buildwithneej

items.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: Google's on-device multimodal embedding model for searching your own files
items.synopsis: Singularity.feed starts from the everyday failure of having 10,000 photos on a phone and no way to find the right one, then introduces Google's free EmbeddingGemma 2 as the model built for exactly that. The explanation avoids jargon: it does not chat, it converts any file into a list of numbers — a pin on a map of meaning — so the word dog, a photo of a dog and the sound of a bark all land in nearly the same place. It spans text, images, audio, video and code, so typing kids laughing jumps straight to that moment in a video with no captions needed, and the full model fits in roughly 567 MB and runs offline.
items.author: singularity.feed

items.title: Aleph Alpha releases Kolibri-1, a German-English open model
items.synopsis: Aleph Alpha has released Kolibri-1, a German-English open-source model that beats Qwen, Nvidia's Nemotron and Mistral Small in its size class on both English and German benchmarks. It was built end to end in Germany, trained on infrastructure in Germany and Finland, and designed around EU AI Act and GDPR requirements. The post frames it as Europe's DeepSeek moment while being explicit that this is not a frontier-level model — rather the strongest homegrown option for European companies that want a capable model they fully control.
items.author: scaling.europe

items.title: Testing Ajax, the abliterated Qwen-based model PewDiePie fine-tuned himself
items.synopsis: Codrkai puts Ajax through its paces — an abliterated model built on Qwen 3.5 9B as its base, trained by the streamer PewDiePie. The backstory matters as much as the model: earlier in the year he built his own agent harness, Odysseus, to run LLMs locally, and it climbed to become one of GitHub's most-downloaded repositories. The reel notes he was subsequently banned from OpenAI over training his own model.
items.author: codrkai

items.title: HyperFrames, an open-source video editor that runs on your own Claude or ChatGPT account
items.synopsis: Lemondedumarketing covers HyperFrames, an open-source editing app sitting above 57,000 GitHub stars, available on Mac and Linux with a Windows build announced. There is no extra subscription — the AI runs against your existing Claude or ChatGPT account — and exports come out at 4K up to 60fps. The caveat he stresses is that the tool supplies no method: editing rules, personal style and what actually holds attention are what his companion guide covers, alongside the limits he hit in testing, and he edited this reel itself with Claude from hook to subtitles.
items.author: lemondedumarketing

items.title: Three files that turn Claude into a co-founder with memory and a voice
items.synopsis: Alassafi.ai describes a three-file setup: a markdown playbook encoding how he runs the company, a memory file holding every deal that persists across sessions, and a voice layer. The voice is an original built in Fish Audio's Voice Design and wired into Claude Code through their MCP with a single command, with emotion tags stacked directly into the generation input — which is why it sounds patient when the schedule holds and annoyed when it slips. He gives a concrete payoff: that morning it told him two developers were blocked and a client had not been updated.
items.author: alassafi.ai

items.title: Impeccable, an open-source design skill that strips the AI tells out of generated sites
items.synopsis: Singularity.feed opens on the recognisable signature of an AI-built website — cream background, fancy serif headline, one photo on the right — and notes the same prompt on the same model produces that same page five runs in a row. The fix offered is Impeccable, a free open-source design skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other agents, installed with npx impeccable install then /impeccable init. For sites that already exist, /polish removes the tells and /distill strips a page back to the single number that matters; running its own detector over the gallery flagged 30 of 35 unpolished Claude pages.
items.author: singularity.feed

items.title: How open source reproduced JEV, a closed decision model, in fourteen days
items.synopsis: Singularity.feed reconstructs the timeline after JEV launched on 15 September as an API-only, closed-weight model that does one narrow thing extremely cheaply: given a question and a short list of answers, it returns one pick plus a calibrated confidence in a single pass, for a fraction of a cent in under half a second — the shape of most real in-app AI work (spam checks, ticket routing, next-action selection). Reproducing it needed no reverse engineering, because the recipe was already public: a researcher had published the idea a year earlier and released an open model three days after JEV, and a Nokia/Tencent team had shown any open model can do it untrained by restricting its next-token scores to the answer letters. The resulting economics explain the flood — one builder trained a copy on a laptop in under two hours, another lab spent about $100 in GPU time — and by day 14 more than 20 open models existed, with OpenAI previewing a Decisions API and Cloudflare and Amazon shipping their own.
items.author: singularity.feed

items.title: Weekly AI roundup: a phone-sized open-source model that runs any task from one prompt
items.synopsis: Leo.synthes leads on a Chinese open-source release billed as the fastest of its kind, able to execute arbitrary tasks on a phone from a single prompt. The rest of the week's digest covers unified memory for agents, Google's Artemis for phone automation, Prism ML's compact Ternary Bonsai 2, AWS's inbox for AI agents, CAI's GLM 5.3 Flash X, and Unsloth Studio's no-code fine-tuning across 500-plus models. The through-line is on-device and open-weight capability closing the gap with hosted frontier models.
items.author: leo.synthes

items.title: Brag turns a Claude Code project into a launch video
items.synopsis: Brag is a free Claude Code skill, already past 5,000 GitHub stars, that generates a finished launch video from a project in a single command. Typing /brag makes it read the entire repository, pick its own marketing angle, decide what to show, and output an animated video complete with music, sound effects and text ready to post. The host notes you can impose a tone such as a fundraising announcement, and suggests it for sales pages, LinkedIn feature launches, or AI consultants presenting a delivered solution to a client.
items.author: simon_de_lima

items.title: Six GitHub repos packaged as sellable AI services
items.synopsis: The carousel collects six open-source GitHub projects and frames each as the basis for a paid service rather than code to resell: Claude Ads for ad auditing, Fincept Terminal for financial systems, Vibe Trading, Camofox Browser for automated browsing, Hyperframes for video at scale, and Open Generative AI for content. The argument is that the tools are free but the value sits in how you package, customise and deliver them. Each entry is listed with its repository URL and a note on the offer it could become.
items.author: techskills

items.title: Meta's Muse agent can read your Instagram saves — including what is inside the videos
items.synopsis: Itstundeanthony tests Muse, Meta's first personal agent, whose differentiator is simply access: no other assistant is wired into your Instagram account. On camera he connects his account and asks whether it can see his saved posts; it confirms, correctly reports 442 saves, and pulls recent ones. The part that convinces him is topical retrieval across the collection — asking for five saved posts about AI, then five saved fashion videos, and verifying against his own account that the returned posts really were ones he had saved.
items.author: itstundeanthony

items.title: Voice Studio clones voices locally across 646 languages
items.synopsis: Voice Studio is an open-source voice-cloning and dubbing tool that has passed 35,000 GitHub stars and runs entirely on the user's own machine. From a short reference recording it clones a voice, then generates voice-overs, audiobooks or dubs any video into one of 646 languages, against roughly 70 for ElevenLabs. Because it runs locally there is no per-character billing and no audio leaves the machine, though the host warns to check each engine's commercial-use terms and to clone only your own voice.
items.author: simon_de_lima

items.title: Cheapest M6 Mac Mini set up as a 24/7 agent host
items.synopsis: The host buys the entry-level M6 Mac Mini specifically to keep AI agents running around the clock, and walks through what that takes beyond installing a single app. Power and sleep settings are changed so the machine stays awake, Tailscale is installed for access from anywhere, then Obsidian, 1Password and Hermes Agent go on to do the actual work. Next steps are a shared memory system called Hindsight so every agent carries the same memory across devices, and migrating the existing setup off an M4 MacBook Pro.
items.author: josephbchandler

items.title: Bonsai 2 squeezes a 27B-parameter model from 55 GB down to 6 GB
items.synopsis: Eliott Meunier covers Bonsai 2 from Prism ML — a company he notes is in acquisition talks with Apple — which compresses Qwen 3.8 27B from a 55 GB file to roughly 6 GB. The method is ternary quantisation, explained from first principles: a model is a mass of stored numbers (weights) carrying several decimal places each, and Bonsai 2 collapses every one of them to just -1, 0 or 1. The surprise is the cost of that brutality — under 2% quality loss on their selected benchmarks — which he reads as evidence that usable local hardware is becoming an optimisation problem rather than a budget one.
items.author: eliott.meunier

items.title: The Generate skill turns Claude into its own Higgsfield-style media stack
items.synopsis: Sebastian Hardy demos a Claude skill called Generate that wires a whole catalogue of third-party image and video models in behind a single conversational interface. The headline behaviour is budget-aware orchestration: ask for ten ads across three image models under three dollars and Claude selects the models, writes each prompt, and price-shops per generation. Every output file is saved alongside the prompt that produced it, so the run stays auditable and reproducible.
items.author: sebastianhardy_

items.title: Google's TimesFM-3 forecasting model, paired with an ontology for business use
items.synopsis: Benoit Ferrere presents TimesFM-3, Google's time-series foundation model, and argues its value inside a company comes from pairing it with a semantic ontology rather than running it bare. He builds the vocabulary up first: a time series is any measure tracked over time (daily sales, stock levels, electricity draw), and forecasting projects that history forward. The pitch rests on two properties — the model is zero-shot, so you hand it your history and it predicts without retraining, and it is multivariate, so it can read several correlated series together.
items.author: benoit.ferrere

items.title: A GitHub list of 130+ AI models usable for free across 40 providers
items.synopsis: A little-known GitHub repository aggregates more than 130 AI models that can be used at zero cost, pulled from 40 different companies including Gemini, Grok and NVIDIA. The creator stresses these are standing free tiers rather than trials that expire the following week, so they remain usable indefinitely. The list plugs into Cursor, Claude Code or Codex in a single click, letting existing tooling fall back onto free models whenever a paid plan cuts off.
items.author: sebastianhardy_

items.title: Jev AI and Laya AI compared side by side
items.synopsis: An image carousel comparing two tools named Jev AI and Laya AI. The caption is a bare five-word label with no criteria, verdict or detail, and as a carousel the post has no audio track to transcribe. What is actually being compared, and on what basis, cannot be determined from the post as saved.
items.author: automatewithmadhav

items.title: Valohai on paying frontier-model prices for jobs a small specialist model does better
items.synopsis: Valohai takes aim at reflexively routing every task to the largest available model, pointing out that the bill arrives fastest on the easy work. The reel lists four such jobs — filling web forms, classifying rows in a table, multivariate forecasting, and picking objects out of an image — and notes a purpose-built specialist model exists for each. The argument is an LLMOps cost one: model choice is an engineering decision, and three of those four specialists can be named in under a minute.
items.author: valohai

items.title: A ten-skill Claude content studio, one skill per stage of production
items.synopsis: The creator runs through ten Claude Skills he uses for content, each owning a distinct stage of the creative process: paper-cut animation, product advertisements, realistic brand content, Vox-style explainer animation, realistic AI characters, full brand commercials, high-converting ads, clean product shots, cinematic product visuals and other creative ad formats. The framing is that together they cover the arc from a first product shot to a finished commercial. His claim is that this is what a creative studio looks like once it fits inside a single window, with the skill files released to commenters.
items.author: mr.pynk

items.title: Harness engineering: why a benchmark score belongs partly to the scaffolding (FR)
items.synopsis: In a 60-second concept explainer, the creator argues that when a lab announces something like 86% on a benchmark, the number is ambiguous because the result can come from the model or from the harness around it. The harness is the layer that acts on the model's decisions - calling tools, fetching data and context, executing the resulting actions - and without it the model never escapes being a plain chatbot. He walks the canonical loop: the model decides it needs a tool, the harness calls it, the result returns to the model, and the model decides again with the new information.
items.author: consti.in.tech

items.title: A public GitHub repo of 4,000+ ready-to-import n8n workflows
items.synopsis: A GitHub repository has collected over 4,000 n8n automation workflows that the creator claims would ordinarily be sold commercially, now freely available. Each workflow is importable by copying its JSON straight into an n8n dashboard, with examples including a YouTube video analyser and a YouTube-to-Shorts converter. Every entry carries notes on the tools, API keys and integrations it needs, and the collection is organised by category - lead generation, email outreach, AI agents - so specific use cases can be found without searching thousands of files.
items.author: ai_vanta_ai

items.title: Xiaomi releases MiMo 2.6 Pro and Flash under MIT with training code and 7,000 environments (FR)
items.synopsis: Xiaomi, better known for smartphones, has released version 2.6 of its MiMo models in two sizes, Pro and Flash, and the creator presents it as a direct blow to American frontier labs. The opening argument is capability - he claims MiMo 2.6 runs close behind the newest Anthropic and OpenAI flagships and ahead of comparable Gemini models - and the second is price, citing roughly 87 US cents per million output tokens, far under American competitors. What makes it notable beyond benchmarks is the openness of the release: published weights, training code, 7,000 training environments and an MIT licence, though he explicitly says the scores need independent verification.
items.author: renauddekode

items.title: Reverse-engineering a real-time webcam fitting room built on Decart's Lucy 2.5 (PT)
items.synopsis: A creative engineer dissects a viral virtual fitting room that generates, live on the user's webcam, video of them wearing garments selected on the site. He identifies it as a product of Decart AI, a startup specialising in low-latency generative models, running their closed, paid Lucy 2.5 model that businesses license and wire into e-commerce or live video to swap scenery and products in real time without post-production. His point is that the capability is no longer rare: JoyAI-Video-Edit from Chinese retail giant JD is an open-source equivalent, and Krea and Vidu both ship comparable products.
items.author: leobeckerdesign

items.title: Voicebox: a free local alternative to ElevenLabs-style voice cloning and dictation (FR)
items.synopsis: Voicebox is a free, open-source GitHub project that covers what ElevenLabs and Whisper-based dictation tools do, but runs entirely on your own machine with no API key and no subscription. It offers voice cloning from a few seconds of audio and speech generation in 23 languages, documented on a full landing page describing the API and the available models. Usage is a single command line: clone a voice, generate the voiceover, and dictate into any text field with a keyboard shortcut.
items.author: matheoct2

items.title: pi-desktop: a persistent local workspace for AI agents
items.synopsis: A desktop application that gives AI agents their own durable workspace rather than ephemeral sessions. Projects and sessions stay local, and cloud or local models can be swapped freely behind the same interface. A plugin system extends it with additional panels and tools.
items.author: githubprojects

items.title: Laya: an Apache-2.0 open-weights answer to Jev's typed-decision API
items.synopsis: Jev replaced generated prose with typed decisions - send a ticket, email or JSON blob and get back a Choice, a Score or a Yes/No with a calibrated probability, no parsing required - but it is closed, with no public weights and no self-hosting, billing every call at $0.042 per million tokens on TypeSafe's servers. The creator's sharper objection is data residency: at thousands of routing decisions a day, every real customer email leaves your infrastructure permanently, decided by weights you cannot inspect or fine-tune. Laya, from Convai Innovations, reproduces the same typed-decision behaviour under Apache 2.0 with open weights, runs entirely on your own hardware at zero marginal cost per decision, and reportedly edges out Jev on a shared benchmark.
items.author: virex.explains

items.title: Motion design from a French prompt: Claude writes the animation, Hyperframe renders it (FR)
items.synopsis: The creator produces three motion-design pieces - a thousand drones drawing his logo over Paris, a 3D Earth tracing a Paris-Tokyo flight, and a self-solving Rubik's Cube - without opening After Effects or writing code, describing each one in French and letting the model code the animation frame by frame. The pipeline's missing half is a free tool called Hyperframe, which converts the generated animation into actual video. He notes a paid Claude subscription is required, and credits the results to a Claude Opus 5.5 release - a version claim made in the reel rather than one verified here.
items.author: lemondedumarketing

items.title: Unlazy: a prompt-level fix aimed at partial compliance in Claude and ChatGPT
items.synopsis: The creator, Stanford founder Ben Gusberg, argues that frontier assistants routinely cut corners and then report the job as finished - behaviour he labels partial compliance, the familiar pattern of an assistant skipping a step and apologising only when challenged. His proposed remedy is a free tool called Unlazy that forces the model to decompose a request into subtasks and give each one full attention, invoked by typing slash Unlazy at the start of a project. Setup is to paste the tool's URL into Claude or ChatGPT and ask it to install; note that the framing that labs deliberately designed models to be lazy and to lie is the creator's claim, not a documented vendor position.
items.author: bengusberg

items.title: Hermes adds a Claude plugin that runs on your subscription, no API key
items.synopsis: A Hermes plugin update reconnects Claude to the agent without requiring an API key or a separate usage bill, running instead on an existing Claude subscription. Users can switch between Opus, Sonnet, Haiku and Fable with a single line, and the creator says installation takes about three minutes via one command. Hermes keeps its memory, tools, browsing and approval flow throughout, so the agent can still read files, browse the web and check its own work inside existing workflows.
items.author: aiprofitlabdaily

items.title: A two-agent content machine turning one product photo into ten on-brand visuals (FR)
items.synopsis: Testing what fully AI-generated brand content is worth in 2026, the creator starts from a single product shot of a New Balance FuelCell v5 plus a moodboard gathered from Pinterest, Cosmos or Google Images. A visual-DNA agent analyses and describes each reference image, then passes its reading to a creative-director agent that writes ten coherent prompts, and the pipeline renders ten usable visuals. His verdict is that this clearly does not replace a real shoot, but earns its place in three cases: zero budget, high volume, or testing visual directions ahead of a production.
items.author: yass.majid

items.title: Pairing the UI UX Pro Max skill with 21st.dev's MCP server in Claude Code
items.synopsis: The setup installs the UI UX Pro Max skill into Claude Code straight from its GitHub URL, giving the model a reference library of over 50 UI styles, 97 colour palettes and 57 font pairings. It then adds 21st.dev's magic MCP server with a single install command. With both in place, Claude Code's generated sites come out with proper animations, glassmorphism, gradients and layouts that look professionally designed rather than default.
items.author: bob.curtis.creator

items.title: STAIR: le RAG d'IBM qui supprime le decoupage en chunks
items.synopsis: STAIR, pour Structure Aware Information Retriever, est une approche de recherche documentaire d'IBM qui se passe entierement de chunking, d'embeddings et de base vectorielle, donc de Qdrant ou Milvus. Plutot que de vectoriser des morceaux, les chercheurs fine-tunent Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 a partir d'un triplet question, sommaire complet et section cible, afin que le modele reponde directement par la reference de la section pertinente, par exemple section 6.3, ce contenu etant ensuite transmis en contexte au LLM generateur. L'hypothese traitee est que les hallucinations naissent en grande partie de frontieres de decoupage arbitraires qui detruisent la structure des longs documents, l'evaluation portant sur dix-huit manuels couvrant six domaines avec une contrepartie assumee cote cout d'entrainement.
items.author: benoit.ferrere

items.title: Nano Jev, la replique open source chinoise de Jev AI
items.synopsis: Le post presente Nano Jev, une replique legere et open source de Jev AI developpee en Chine et deja creditee d'environ deux mille etoiles sur GitHub. Son argument differenciant est la prise de decisions en parallele: on lui soumet plusieurs choix et il les arbitre simultanement, le tout gratuitement. L'auteur le positionne comme brique a integrer dans des workflows d'agents et d'automatisation, et renvoie le mode d'emploi complet vers le lien en bio.
items.author: julian.goldie_

items.title: needle: a 45M-parameter foundation model in a 14MB binary for phones and robots
items.synopsis: needle, from cactus-compute, packs a 45-million-parameter foundation model into a single 14MB binary that runs entirely offline on phones, wearables and robots. Quantised to 2 bits it needs roughly 28MB of RAM and is 5 to 70 times smaller than comparable models such as FunctionGemma. It takes text in and emits JSON out with tool calling built in, and ships under Apache-2.0.
items.author: fullstackparody

items.title: Teaser sur une IA sans filtre, gratuite et non nommee
items.synopsis: Le createur annonce l'existence d'une IA gratuite fonctionnant sans censure ni garde-fou, capable selon lui de repondre a n'importe quelle question. Le propos reste au stade de l'avertissement moral, puisqu'il souligne lui-meme le risque entre de mauvaises mains, sans jamais nommer le service, le modele sous-jacent ni en montrer une sortie concrete. Le lien est conditionne au commentaire FILTRE, ce qui rend la publication non verifiable: ni la bande-son ni la legende ne permettent d'identifier le produit presente.
items.author: jeremy_ia

items.title: Six markdown context files that keep an AI coding agent on the rails
items.synopsis: The post prescribes six markdown files to commit at the start of any vibe-coding project so the agent inherits durable context instead of re-guessing it every session. They are prd.md (what is being built, for whom, which features), architecture.md (file and folder layout, tech stack, how the parts connect), rules.md (a rulebook of libraries, error handling and constraints), design.md (colours, typography, components and spacing so the UI stays consistent), tasks.md (the project split into small units handed to the agent one at a time), and memory.md (running project context). The framing is tool-agnostic across Claude Code and Cursor, and the caption enumerates all six files even though a fuller step-by-step guide sits behind a comment gate.
items.author: avani.codes

items.title: Jev AI part two: Jevpilot, a Subway Surfers agent, and 700 leads scored for nine cents
items.synopsis: The creator frames Jev as the yin to an LLM's yang - where a language model writes, Jev makes fast decisions inside your computer. Three demos carry the reel: Jevpilot, a Tesla-style self-driving agent that stops at a red light and resumes on green; a Subway Surfers player choosing lanes, jumps and slides with near-superhuman reaction; and a sales tool that assessed 700 leads and their outreach messages in 40 seconds. That last run reportedly cost nine cents, letting a team catch bad-fit messages before they are ever sent.
items.author: brochbuilds

items.title: From a stranger's camo pants to ordered samples: Aria turns one photo into a tech pack
items.synopsis: The creator photographs a passer-by's camo trousers, feeds the image to an app whose assistant is called Aria, and uses the generated template to redesign them as cargo shorts with custom front pockets. Aria then produces the tech pack - the manufacturing spec sheet - capturing nearly every detail needed for production. Asked to find a manufacturer, it returns several viable options, and the creator orders samples and shows the finished shorts, all from a single image.
items.author: tchpack.studio

items.title: Seedance 2.5 re-shoots one take from four camera angles without reshooting
items.synopsis: A technique for generating multiple camera angles from a single existing take using Seedance 2.5, so the same footage yields different distances and scales without anything being shot twice. The workflow is to note every timecode where the camera should cut, hand those timecodes and desired angles to Claude to compose the prompt, then run it in Seedance 2.5 with the original video uploaded as reference. The step the author says people skip is explicitly instructing the model to preserve location, dialogue and action, without which it reinvents the scene entirely, and he advises generating one angle at a time rather than expecting a single pass to land.
items.author: dash.werk

items.title: Open-source script-to-video pipeline that renders a full production (tool unnamed)
items.synopsis: The reel demonstrates an open-source video tool that takes a written script and returns a finished production, handling characters, episodes, scenes, storyboard, voiceover, editing and final export in one automated chain. Because it is open source it can be run locally, and the creator says short drama ads and product videos are the main uses so far. The tool is never named in either the caption or the audio - the link is released only to commenters - so the specific project cannot be identified from this post.
items.author: sebintel

items.title: Day 2 of a local-LLM Tamagotchi: a Raspberry Pi 5 thin client over WebSocket streaming
items.synopsis: In the second instalment of building an oversized Tamagotchi around a self-hosted LLM, the creator keeps all computation on a dedicated server and adds a Raspberry Pi 5 as the client that talks to Luna, the local model. Latency is the binding constraint because Luna is meant to become a voice assistant, so the build uses a WebSocket plus token streaming combo: the server listens continuously and the reply renders word by word instead of waiting for the full sentence. The next problem flagged is memory - Luna currently forgets everything when the client is powered off.
items.author: theshalaulabs

items.title: Recreating any film's look from one phone take, via a Claude skill and Seedance 2.5
items.synopsis: The claim is that a single phone take can be restyled into the look of any named film, series or director — not as a colour filter, but by rebuilding the lighting, camera work and scene. The workflow runs a Claude skill over the footage, which transcribes the take with precise timestamps and writes the full prompt automatically, encoding the film's lighting and the director's camera moves with cuts landing word by word against the speech. That prompt and the original video then go into Seedance 2.5, replacing what the creator says previously required a colourist, a DP and a set.
items.author: pauloshimas

items.title: oMLX: running local LLMs fast on Apple Silicon and wiring them into Hermes
items.synopsis: A Mac-only setup walkthrough for oMLX, a local inference server that optimizes models for Apple Silicon via the MLX framework, installed from a DMG published on the project's GitHub releases page. After setting an API key as the admin password, the built-in model downloader pulls a Qwen 3.5 9B checkpoint, which the author tests on a multi-stock web-search prompt that returns a sourced answer in about three minutes. The second half connects the server to the Hermes desktop client as a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint at localhost:8000/v1, and the author rates oMLX above comparable MLX servers he tried for its context-window handling and automatic model downloads on a 32 GB M2 Pro.
items.author: codrkai

items.title: Running a 744B-parameter model on a laptop with no GPU, via the Calibri project
items.synopsis: An Italian developer ran GLM 5.2 — a 744-billion-parameter open model — on a laptop with no graphics card, using a project called Calibri. It works because only around 10 GB of the model is active at any moment, so Calibri holds that slice in RAM and streams the rest off disk on demand, the way a video service streams rather than downloading. Setup is cloning the repo and running one script; the heavy part is the 370 GB model download, after which it runs fully offline, and a serve mode exposes it as an OpenAI-compatible endpoint so a one-line code change drops your token bill to zero.
items.author: ai_vanta_ai

items.title: Higgsfield Genjutsu keeps the motion and swaps everyone in the frame (FR)
items.synopsis: Genjutsu, Higgsfield's new model, preserves the movement of a source video while replacing the person, the objects and the entire set around them. The reel opens with staged scam scenarios - a fake distressed relative asking for 800 euros, a bogus anti-fraud agent, an invented doctor pushing a supplement - to show that the lip-sync desynchronisation, blurred contours and vanishing details that used to betray AI video are essentially gone. The creator's position is that the result is stunning for advertising and film but alarming for fraud, and that testing these tools is the only way to understand either side.
items.author: ninon.ia_officiel

items.title: Abliterated Qwen 3.8 run locally through the Hermes agent
items.synopsis: A walkthrough of an abliterated, uncensored build of the open-source Qwen 3.8 model, downloaded from Hugging Face and driven locally through the Hermes Agent in LM Studio. The author tests the unrestricted variant against prompts a guardrailed model would refuse, positioning it as a fully local alternative with no API dependency. The practical catch is hardware: the post recommends substantial VRAM or a Mac Studio with 96GB and preferably 128GB of memory, noting it will run on a 32GB machine but slowly.
items.author: codrkai

items.title: 7 codes slash pour piloter la generation d'images de GPT-Image-2
items.synopsis: Le createur presente sept mots-cles courts, ecrits comme des commandes slash, qui orientent GPT-Image-2 vers des concepts visuels que le modele maitrise deja: vue eclatee piece par piece, coupe en deux revelant le mecanisme, rendu radiographique, plan technique facon blueprint, ingredients etiquetes, page de carnet manuscrite et miniature YouTube. L'argument de fond est que depuis GPT-Image-2 le modele raisonne avant de dessiner, donc un mot-concept produit un rendu plus net qu'un paragraphe descriptif ecrit a la main. Les codes se combinent entre eux, par exemple /xray puis /blueprint sur le resultat, mais la liste complete des cinquante reste reservee aux commentaires.
items.author: lemondedumarketing

items.title: Open Art turns one sentence into a directed explainer video
items.synopsis: The whole demo video began from the single prompt “explain gravity”, with every subsequent refinement handled through conversation rather than a timeline. Testing it live on “explain recursion in a 30-second video”, the creator finds the tool generates a storyboard with GPT Image 2 and the audio track with Lyria, behind a paywall he ends up subscribing to. A second run explaining inflation in an anime style — which it chose to render in Spanish — also lands, and he rates it a “fact”.
items.author: itstundeanthony

items.title: screenshot-to-code: the GitHub repo that clones a website from an image properly
items.synopsis: The creator tests a repo called screenshot to code against the usual failure mode, where handing Claude a reference link produces something that barely resembles the original. After cloning the repo and adding environment variables, he runs a Crunchyroll clone through it and races the same task against Claude Code for comparison. The repo's output is clearly better — it correctly grabbed the logo and used the actual cover art — earning a “fact” verdict.
items.author: itstundeanthony

items.title: Why AI twins look fake: curated selfies vs a live 100-shot capture
items.synopsis: Most AI clone models ask you to upload photos, so people submit their five best shots and the model learns only their five best angles, returning a person who exists solely at those angles. This tool replaces uploads with a live camera capture of roughly 100 frames taken while you turn your head, including the unflattering up, down and side angles nobody would choose. The creator concedes the capture is uncomfortable even for her, and argues that discomfort is precisely the feature that makes the output read as a person rather than a stock photo.
items.author: nauraissues

items.title: Wiring an Obsidian vault into Claude Desktop through the Docker MCP catalog
items.synopsis: Codrkai screen-records the full setup for letting Claude read and write an Obsidian vault, starting from installing Obsidian, creating the vault folder and letting it map whatever files are dropped in. The bridge is the community plugin Local REST API with MCP, which exposes an API key (the key only, not the Bearer prefix) that is then pasted as a secret into Docker Desktop's MCP Tools catalog, where the Obsidian server is enabled, added to a profile and attached to the Claude Desktop client. Verification is done from Claude Desktop under customize connectors, where the vault appears behind the MCP Docker connector, after which Claude can be asked to organise the vault or file chats and code into it.
items.author: codrkai

items.title: OpenWA: a self-hosted, MIT-licensed WhatsApp API with no per-message fees
items.synopsis: OpenWA is an open-source WhatsApp API you deploy on your own server with a single Docker command, removing the per-message billing of the official Business API. One instance handles unlimited WhatsApp accounts and exposes messages, media, reactions and bulk sends through a REST API, with webhooks, a React dashboard and audit logs included. It is MIT licensed with a pluggable backend, so there is no middleman between the sender and the platform.
items.author: marc.kaz

items.title: SubQ claims the first frontier model that drops the Transformer
items.synopsis: A Miami startup called SubQ claims to have shipped the first frontier model not built on the Transformer, targeting dense self-attention's O(n squared) cost — every token compared against every other token, so doubling the input quadruples the compute, a tax every model has paid since 2017. Its approach, sub-quadratic sparse attention, has each token dynamically attend only to the most relevant others, pushing scaling closer to linear and yielding a claimed native 12-million-token context window, roughly 52x faster than flash attention at 1M tokens and about a fifth the cost of GPT-5.5 or Claude Opus on long-context work. The post closes on its own caveat: no independent party has benchmarked SubQ on long-context tasks that matter, the model is in private beta, and Transformers have survived every architectural challenge for nine years — though the wall it attacks is real.
items.author: poojaduttttt

items.title: Four European model releases in twenty-four hours
items.synopsis: The carousel catalogues an unusually dense day for European AI, naming each release and its claim. Mistral announced Le Chonk, described as the best open-weights model from the US or Europe on aggregated benchmarks, while Aleph Alpha released Kolibri-1, a benchmark-beating open-source model. ElevenLabs v4 Turbo topped the text-to-speech benchmarks and Black Forest Labs FLUX 3 was named the strongest world model, which the author reads as a turning point for European AI.
items.author: scaling.europe

items.title: An autonomous-driving week and an Italian security unicorn
items.synopsis: A short VC note calling it an exciting week for autonomous driving and congratulating a new cybersecurity unicorn working on physical AI, flagged as Italian. Neither company is named in the caption. The specifics are in the video.
items.author: chrissy.vc

items.title: Seven slash-codes that steer ChatGPT image editing
items.synopsis: Limor Markman walks through seven short "slash codes" appended to the end of a ChatGPT prompt, each one pinning the model to a specific photo-editing job rather than leaving the interpretation open. The list runs /photo restore for faded or torn family pictures, /professional retouch, /background change, /object remove, /golden hour for warm low-sun relighting, and /professional portrait to give a phone selfie headshot framing and lighting. The one she flags as non-negotiable is /identity preserve — without it, she argues, successive edits drift the subject's face into someone else's, so it belongs in every single request; a fuller catalogue of around a hundred codes sits behind a "Comment IMAGE" DM gate.
items.author: limor_markman

items.title: Prompt de caricature numerique joyeuse pour Gemini
items.synopsis: Carrousel presentant un prompt d'edition photo destine a Gemini, qui transforme un portrait en caricature numerique d'allure joyeuse et cartoon. La legende se limite a une ligne de description et a une poignee de hashtags, sans exposer le texte du prompt ni les reglages employes. Le post ne comporte pas de piste audio, donc aucune transcription ne peut en completer le contenu.

As a still-image carousel with no audio track, there is no voiceover from which the missing technique could be recovered.

items.title: Pixlr's Cinematic Light effect adds film-style lighting in one click
items.synopsis: Pixlr's Cinematic Light effect relights an existing photo with dramatic, film-inspired lighting rather than a flat filter pass. It introduces moody shadows, glowing highlights and a sense of depth that ordinary edits cannot reproduce. Pixlr positions it for portraits and product shots, with the underlying prompt available on request.

The prompts themselves are withheld behind a comment gate, so only the output and the tool name are public.

items.title: Motion-as-language image prompts: blur, ghosting, refraction, chromatic drag
items.synopsis: A Portuguese-language carousel of prompts built deliberately around motion artefacts — motion blur, ghosting, refraction, smear, chromatic distortion and panning — treating movement as part of the image visual grammar rather than a defect to avoid. The creator frames it as an alternative path to the clean, static look that dominates AI imagery. Full prompt text is offered by DM, and a paid product is plugged alongside.

items.title: Prompt-library teaser for an AI content workflow (caption-gated)

items.title: Four prompts for the 1980s fashion portrait trend, usable with your own photo
items.synopsis: A carousel responding to the wave of 1980s-styled AI portraits circulating on Instagram, offering four distinct prompts that each produce a different variation of the look. The creator specifies that the prompts are designed to be combined with a user-supplied reference photo rather than generating a stranger. The prompt text itself is delivered by DM on comment.
items.author: ertanlabs

items.title: Le réalisme 8K ne s'obtient pas en écrivant 8K dans le prompt
items.synopsis: L'auteur explique que le vrai détail 8K ne vient jamais du mot 8K placé dans le prompt, mais d'une reconstruction spécifiée à chaque niveau de zoom. Il énumère les marqueurs à décrire explicitement : profondeur des fibres de l'iris et anneau limbique de l'œil, brillance de sébum sur le nez, bordure vermillon de la lèvre, duvet se détachant de la joue et lumière courant le long de chaque cheveu. Le principe est que chaque niveau de recadrage réclame sa propre instruction, les cinq prompts complets restant réservés à ceux qui commentent 8K.
items.author: its.mrpickard

items.title: Avatar prompt set offered by DM, no method shown
items.synopsis: A carousel of AI avatar images whose caption consists solely of a request to comment AVATAR in exchange for the prompts. No generator, workflow or prompt structure appears anywhere in the post. The images are the only substantive content, making this a pure distribution mechanic.

items.title: Stacking prompt fragments instead of firing single AI “codes”

The post shows the slot structure itself but keeps the worked examples behind a follow-and-save call to action.

items.title: Street-art style AI portrait (prompt gated)

items.title: Portrait transforme en couverture de comic vintage

Le post est une vitrine de resultat : trames, aplats et typographie retro sont obtenus sans illustrateur ni encrage, uniquement via un prompt d'image. Le prompt exact n'est pas publie et reste conditionne a un commentaire, ce qui limite la valeur technique reutilisable de la publication.
items.author: steal.prompts

items.title: Same AI model, different camera angles as a controllable variable
items.synopsis: A carousel showing one consistent AI-generated model photographed from a series of different camera positions, making the case that camera specification alone substantially changes the output. The practical point is that angle is a prompt-level control worth isolating rather than leaving to the generator. The accompanying prompts and guide are offered by DM on comment.
items.author: ankitgraphic

items.title: Pop-art illustration portrait (prompt gated)
items.synopsis: A carousel showing an AI-generated portrait styled as a pop-art illustration with bold flat colour and heavy outlines. The caption names the style and asks for a comment to receive the prompt by DM, disclosing no model or technique. Being an image carousel there is no audio to transcribe, leaving the visual reference as the only usable signal.
items.author: paige.prompts

items.title: UPSCALE : un seul prompt pour nettoyer et rehausser une photo
items.synopsis: @prompts.soul presente un prompt unique baptise UPSCALE qui prend en charge tout le post-traitement d'une photo existante plutot que d'en generer une nouvelle. Le prompt vise une montee en resolution accompagnee d'un etalonnage precis : verts profonds, hautes lumieres d'heure doree, ciel bleu propre, carnations naturelles et blancs neutres. L'auteur insiste sur ce qu'il refuse - pas de lissage plastique de la peau, pas de halos de faux piquer - en preservant grain, texture de peau et details capillaires ; le prompt lui-meme reste accessible en commentaire.
items.author: prompts.soul

items.title: Eight cinematic lighting prompts as a saveable reference
items.synopsis: A carousel presenting eight lighting setups framed as the lever that makes AI visuals read as cinematic rather than flat. The eight full prompts are sent by DM in exchange for a comment.
items.author: akashgraphxic

items.title: Caricature-style AI character portraits, prompt by numbered comment
items.synopsis: A Persian-language carousel showing stylised caricature character portraits generated from personal photos, pitched at profile-picture use. items.title: Hyper-realistic photo prompts offered on comment

items.title: Ultra-realistic profile-photo prompt pitched against bad selfies
items.synopsis: A Brazilian-Portuguese carousel contrasting poorly lit phone selfies with AI-generated portrait alternatives, promising results that avoid the tell-tale AI look. items.title: Vintage editorial photography style, prompts by comment
items.synopsis: A Spanish-language carousel showcasing a vintage editorial photography aesthetic applied to AI-generated portraits. items.title: One photo into twelve ages: an age-progression sheet from 5 to 80
items.synopsis: Phil shares a prompt pair that takes a single uploaded photo and returns one sheet showing the same person at twelve ages, running 5, 8, 12, 16, 20, 25 then 30, 40, 50, 60, 70 and 80. He explains the trick is instructing the model to lock the subject's bone structure and age only skin, fat and hair, which keeps it recognisably one person across the sheet rather than twelve unrelated faces. He provides separate men's and women's variants, the men's version also ageing the stubble, and runs the whole thing in Picsart Flow on GPT Image 2.
items.author: ai.withphil

items.title: “Old money” cinematic portrait prompt, gated behind a comment
items.synopsis: A carousel of portraits in the old-money aesthetic — muted palette, heritage tailoring, soft cinematic grade. The caption is a one-line lead magnet offering the prompts by DM on comment. No generator, reference-image workflow or prompt structure is disclosed in the post itself.
items.author: prompty.ai

items.title: 20 prompt recipes turning clothing photos into fashion campaign shots
items.synopsis: A carousel of twenty prompt recipes aimed at apparel sellers, converting flat product photography into model shoots, lookbooks, seasonal collections, bridal campaigns and in-store displays. The pitch is that a brand can generate campaign-grade imagery from garment photos it already owns rather than commissioning a shoot. The carousel frames each use case but routes the detailed prompt text to the creator channel.

items.title: 99 viral image prompts for ChatGPT, presented as a save-and-try list
items.synopsis: A high-engagement carousel compiling ninety-nine short image prompts for ChatGPT, organised loosely by style, effect, lighting and photography genre. Unusually for the format the post is a save-this rather than a DM-gate, so the prompt list is intended to be read straight from the slides. The prompts are keyword-style rather than structured, aimed at breadth over control.

items.title: 100+ shorthand ChatGPT image prompts, gated behind a comment
items.synopsis: A rapid before/after reel cycling through image results, each narrated only as type this, get this against a shorthand prompt. Neither the caption nor the audio names a technique, model setting or reasoning, so the whole post works as a delivery hook for a pack of 100+ ChatGPT image prompts sent by DM on comment. The visible outputs suggest short keyword-style prompts for stylised images, but nothing in the post is specific enough to reconstruct.
