items.title: Gaussian splatting to take back camera control in an AI image workflow
items.synopsis: Paint Motion Pictures shows an early test that grew into the technique he calls Paint Scan: capturing a 3D Gaussian splat of his own face and pairing it with a high-resolution character reference sheet. The combination lets him generate new images at the exact camera angle, composition and pose he wants while holding facial fidelity, independent of the environment he places himself in. He highlights un-promptable poses as the real unlock, since shots he would not know how to describe in words can now be pulled in as reference and re-framed later.
items.author: paintmotionpictures

items.title: Nine ChatGPT prompts that restyle a phone photo as a professional shoot
items.synopsis: The carousel argues that ChatGPT's image editing is now good enough to make an ordinary phone photo read as a professional studio or location shoot, with no camera or editing skill involved. It enumerates nine prompt recipes: DSLR photographer mode, cinematic photoshoot, luxury Instagram look, travel influencer shots, magazine cover style, old photo restoration, location swaps, professional headshots and golden hour glow. The stated use cases are LinkedIn headshots, travel-style content without travelling, and a more premium-looking feed; the prompt text itself is delivered by DM.

items.title: An open-source pipeline for transferring real facial emotion into AI video
items.synopsis: Sirio tackles emotion control for AI filmmaking, showing first why the obvious approach fails: Claude and Codex both built Hollywood-style facial-landmark dot masks, but stripped of the source video the masks are unreadable, with a crying performance rendering as laughter. His fix layers FLAME, a reshapeable 3D face model, with SPECTRE chosen over SMIRK for better mouth and lip reconstruction, then corrects the mask frame by frame against the tracked points. Grayscale detail from the original footage is blended back around the eyes and lips and directional light plus clay materials are added, producing a conditioning input for Seedance that does not guarantee an exact copy but gives the model a far more specific performance to follow; the pipeline is open-sourced and gated behind a 'workflow' comment.

items.title: A five-tool local stack that lets Claude Code edit video end to end
items.synopsis: Kappa.ai lays out the toolchain behind "Claude edits my videos", distributed as a single file you drop into Claude Code that installs everything itself, runs locally on Mac or Windows, and needs no API keys or extra subscriptions. The pieces are HyperFrames as the video engine where the project lives (Remotion works in its place if you already use it), Whisper so Claude transcribes every word and places subtitles on time, CLAP so it can identify each sound and find similar ones in your library, Demucs to split a track into voice, drums, bass and the rest, and Blender so 3D objects are built locally instead of burning credits per shot. Once installed, the workflow is to describe the video you want and let Claude start cutting; an existing Higgsfield subscription can optionally be connected on top.

items.title: Turning a creator's editing style into a Claude Code skill and 12-step SOP

A second prompt converts that document into a Claude skill encoding a twelve-step standard operating procedure, which then takes raw footage, proposes a storyboard for approval, and drafts and reviews its own edit until animation and timing match. items.title: LTX 2.5 ships open weights with audio and video generated in one pass
items.synopsis: LTX 2.5 is an open-weights video model, free to download and run locally on an ordinary Mac or Windows machine, which the post credits with 18 million downloads as evidence it works in practice. The feature it leads on is generating audio and video in a single pass, removing the usual step of stitching a voiceover onto a silent clip. It also holds multi-shot sequences, keeping character and lighting consistent across cuts where most AI video tools reset between renders and leave you matching mismatched clips by hand, and it is offered either as downloadable weights or through an API.

It also notes that cloud coding agents are already trained on these tools, so the editing can be automated rather than learned by hand.

items.title: Open-source reconstruction of Higgsfield's Genjutsu video pipeline
items.synopsis: Sirio reverse-engineers Higgsfield's Genjutsu effect and open-sources the whole pipeline: the uploaded video's audio is split into voice and music stems, the music is muted and the voice pitched up three semitones, then Video Depth Anything applies a depth mask from which the subject is segmented and laid back over the original footage. A mesh mask tracking over 478 points is generated alongside and saved as JSON, and the merged segmentation plus inputs are passed to Seedance for generation — the subject being unrecognisable and the voice pitched is what keeps the output clear of copyrighted likeness — before the original audio is restored at the end. He ships a GitHub repo, a simple UI, a tutorial and an agent skill; the only paid dependency is a Seedance enhancer API key, and he notes the same segment-and-replace workflow generalises to swapping any background or object.

He sketches the wider stack around it — ElevenLabs for voiceover and sound effects, Remotion and Hyperframe for motion design — and notes the prompt behind this one was deliberately basic.

items.title: Blackmagic Camera settings for cinematic iPhone footage
items.synopsis: Episode two of a mobile cinematography series walks through the exact Blackmagic Camera app configuration for filming on an iPhone: 24 fps for the cinematic cadence and a 180-degree shutter for natural motion blur, both locked and never touched again. White balance goes to automatic outside controlled setups, while ISO is treated as the critical dial because raising it introduces grain, which is why the previous episode recommended an ND filter. The creator notes the workflow applies to iPhone Pro and Pro Max models from the 15 onward, with backend settings and a LUT reserved for commenters.
items.author: jesserydr

items.title: Drop the Higgsfield subscription: Kie.ai aggregation plus Seedance 2.5 and GPT Image 2
items.synopsis: This French reel argues that a Higgsfield subscription is an unnecessary cost and proposes routing generation through Kie.ai instead, which aggregates the major image and video models on a shared credit pool. The presenter's picks are GPT Image 2 for stills and Seedance 2.5 for video, which he characterises as close to text-to-Hollywood-film quality. The final step wires the whole thing into Claude Code in the terminal via an Orca setup and a supplied master prompt, so a single agent can generate website, e-book, course and content assets on demand - though that prompt is itself comment-gated.
items.author: bariqrifki

items.title: Seedance 2.5 re-shoots one take from four camera angles without reshooting
items.synopsis: A technique for generating multiple camera angles from a single existing take using Seedance 2.5, so the same footage yields different distances and scales without anything being shot twice. The workflow is to note every timecode where the camera should cut, hand those timecodes and desired angles to Claude to compose the prompt, then run it in Seedance 2.5 with the original video uploaded as reference. The step the author says people skip is explicitly instructing the model to preserve location, dialogue and action, without which it reinvents the scene entirely, and he advises generating one angle at a time rather than expecting a single pass to land.
items.author: dash.werk

items.title: Google Flow turns a flat business poster into a 3D motion graphic
items.synopsis: The reel demonstrates a one-minute workflow that animates any static promotional poster into a cinematic 3D motion graphic using Google Flow. The recipe is deliberately minimal: upload the flat poster image, paste a single supplied prompt, and generate - the model infers depth, camera movement and product-shot framing from the artwork alone. The actual prompt and a step-by-step guide are published in a linked Google Doc rather than gated behind a comment, so the technique is fully reproducible from the post itself.
items.author: thefhd.ai

items.title: Cinq commandes Google Flow pour transformer une photo produit en video marketing
items.synopsis: Le reel enumere cinq commandes Google Flow orientees marketing produit qui evitent d'ecrire de longs prompts : smoke reveal pour un devoilement dramatique du produit, Times Square 3D reveal pour l'inserer dans une scene publicitaire 3D a Times Square, et UGC product hook pour generer une video de promotion facon createur de contenu. Les deux autres, miniature product world et POV product demo, construisent respectivement un micro-univers cinematographique autour du produit et une demonstration realiste en vue subjective. L'auteur annonce un guide de plus de 100 commandes du meme type, accessible en commentant FLOW.
items.author: marketerhub.ai

items.title: Open-source script-to-video pipeline that renders a full production (tool unnamed)
items.synopsis: The reel demonstrates an open-source video tool that takes a written script and returns a finished production, handling characters, episodes, scenes, storyboard, voiceover, editing and final export in one automated chain. Because it is open source it can be run locally, and the creator says short drama ads and product videos are the main uses so far. The tool is never named in either the caption or the audio - the link is released only to commenters - so the specific project cannot be identified from this post.
items.author: sebintel

items.title: A 15-second cinematic latte ad built from eight GPT Image keyframes and Seedance 2.5
items.synopsis: The creator documents an end-to-end AI product commercial: eight cinematic keyframes generated with GPT Image around a deliberate sequence of drop, wave, milk collision, marble, swirl, pour, cream crown and hero shot. Product consistency — same cup, branding, ice and strawberry pieces — was held across every frame, then Seedance 2.5 animated the eight stills into one continuous take joined by liquid-motion transitions. The stated lesson is that the visual progression has to be planned up front, because good individual frames alone will not cut together.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Cinq commandes de camera Google Flow pour animer une image fixe
items.synopsis: Le reel montre comment transformer une simple image importee dans Google Flow en plan cinematographique grace a cinq commandes slash : /dolly in rapproche physiquement la camera du sujet pour une tension que le zoom ne reproduit pas, /low angle place la camera sous le sujet pour une perspective dominante, et /slide tracking fait glisser la camera le long du sujet en mouvement facon scene de poursuite hollywoodienne. Les deux dernieres, /360 reveal et /slow motion, ajoutent respectivement un mouvement circulaire complet avec reveal dramatique et un etirement temporel donnant un effet onirique. L'auteure precise qu'il s'agit de 5 commandes sur 50 et renvoie vers la liste complete par DM en commentant FLOW.
items.author: lisaworldverse

items.title: Recreating any film's look from one phone take, via a Claude skill and Seedance 2.5
items.synopsis: The claim is that a single phone take can be restyled into the look of any named film, series or director — not as a colour filter, but by rebuilding the lighting, camera work and scene. The workflow runs a Claude skill over the footage, which transcribes the take with precise timestamps and writes the full prompt automatically, encoding the film's lighting and the director's camera moves with cuts landing word by word against the speech. That prompt and the original video then go into Seedance 2.5, replacing what the creator says previously required a colourist, a DP and a set.
items.author: pauloshimas

items.title: GPT 6 Astra contre Fable 5.1: un montage video complet en un seul prompt
items.synopsis: L'auteur soumet un meme rush brut et un meme prompt a deux modeles, GPT 6 Astra et Fable 5.1, en one-shot et sans aucune retouche humaine, puis compare les deux montages generes. Il detaille les epreuves qui discriminent vraiment: gestion de la mise en page, ou Astra construit un overlay et repousse le sujet a droite quand Fable conserve le cadrage, sous-titres synchronises mot a mot, citation a illustrer, avant-apres en split screen, classement anime et zoom ancre sur un mot precis. Le test le plus revelateur est negatif: savoir ne rien afficher quand une phrase n'a pas besoin de graphique, et rappeler en fin de video un chiffre annonce au debut, ce qui prouve que le modele a suivi tout le rush et pas une seule ligne.
items.author: withpt.ai

items.title: Five camera-move commands for Google Flow image-to-video
items.synopsis: A Spanish-language reel demonstrating five camera-motion keywords to type alongside an uploaded still in Google Flow: Dolly In for a smooth push toward the subject, Arc Left for a lateral orbit keeping the character centred, Overhead for a cinematic top-down angle, Crash Zoom for an aggressive snap-in, and a crane-up command for a rising shot. Each is shown applied to the same source image so the motion difference is visible. The post is a teaser for a PDF of 50+ such commands delivered by DM on comment, but the five demonstrated here are usable as-is.
items.author: luigivera.y

items.title: A fully automated French short: Claude Code writes it, HyperFrames renders it
items.synopsis: In a “pro ou mytho” verdict format, the creator reveals the short being shown features neither his face, his voice, his script, his edit nor his design work. The pipeline runs Claude Code from a terminal to write the video as code, HyperFrames to build it shot by shot, and a scheduler to publish weeks ahead — he notes he substituted HyperFrames for the more expensive tool in the technique he was copying. His verdict is that the workflow genuinely works.
items.author: jarod.le.cameleon

items.title: Italian comment-gated giveaway of an AI prompt pack
items.synopsis: A carousel post in Italian whose caption is purely a lead magnet: comment 'PROMPT' and the creator sends the complete pack for free. The visuals show AI-generated output but neither the model nor the prompts are named. The hashtags place it in the generic AI-creator trend space rather than describing any specific tool.
items.author: akapepinho

items.title: GPT-6 Astra plus free HyperFrames as a CapCut replacement for Reels
items.synopsis: The creator claims the reel itself was edited end to end by GPT-6 Astra — cuts, subtitles, motion design and sound effects — with no manual editing. The stack is two pieces: a paid ChatGPT plan (the €20 tier suffices) for Astra, which writes the animation as code, and the free HyperFrames tool, which renders that code into actual video. The caption adds the quota economics: Astra burns through a Plus quota fast in Codex, so the advice is to have Astra plan the edit and hand execution to the cheaper GPT-5.6 Sol.
items.author: lemondedumarketing

items.title: New camera angles from footage you already shot, using Krea and Seedance 2.5
items.synopsis: The workflow starts by deciding which parts of an existing video must stay fixed and which shots or camera moves you want to add. The source video is then uploaded to Krea as a reference with Seedance 2.5 selected, and the prompt explicitly pins the constants — characters, actions, overall scene — while describing the new angles and movements. A few minutes later the same scene returns with different camera work, without regenerating the shot from scratch.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Higgsfield Genjutsu: motion transfer and selective object swap in video
items.synopsis: Genjutsu is presented as a control-first alternative to blanket AI video swap tools, offering two distinct modes. Motion transfer preserves the original movement, camera path and timing while replacing everything else; object swap changes only the element you select and leaves the rest of the frame untouched. The demonstrated workflow is deliberately short — open Genjutsu, pick a mode, upload your video plus references, hit generate — with the link gated behind a comment.
items.author: higgsfield.ai

items.title: Deux commandes Google Flow pour décliner une photo produit en publicités
items.synopsis: La démonstration part d'une seule image produit chargée dans Google Flow, puis utilise des commandes slash pour en tirer plusieurs formats publicitaires. La commande /UGC ad transforme l'image en publicité de style créateur et ajoute même un personnage cohérent avec le produit, tandis que /luxury ad produit une publicité cinématographique haut de gamme. L'auteur annonce plus de cinquante autres commandes produit du même type, envoyées en message privé à qui commente PRODUCT.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Generating a synthetic AI influencer through a Claude custom connector
items.synopsis: Hugo Matias opens by revealing the woman on screen is entirely AI-generated, then walks through reproducing her: copy an MCP server link, add it in the Claude settings as a custom connector, rename it and continue. A single prompt then returns a consistent AI influencer persona in about two minutes. The rest of the pitch is monetisation, posting the output to social platforms for reach and redirecting that traffic to a paid fan platform, with the full method gated behind a comment; the connector name is only spoken aloud, so the exact tool is not reliably identifiable from the video.
items.author: hugomatias.ai

items.title: Turning one talking-head take into an eight-camera studio shoot
items.synopsis: Nomada Toast demonstrates converting a single flat talking-head recording into footage that looks shot by a full studio camera rig. The workflow starts with a screenshot of the original take, runs it through an image generator to rebuild the scene as a professional studio, adding props with the pen tool or command-clicking to alter elements, then imports the original video alongside that still. Seedance 2.5 inside Lovart transforms the whole recording against the new reference, turning one shot into roughly eight distinct angles without reshooting.
items.author: nomadatoast

items.title: Free open-source cinematic video generation with sound
items.synopsis: The creator dropped paid AI video subscriptions after finding a free open-source alternative. It generates cinematic video with sound effects from either text or images. Camera movement, effects, styles and scenes are controllable, and running it locally removes any cap on generations.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Open Art turns one sentence into a directed explainer video
items.synopsis: The whole demo video began from the single prompt “explain gravity”, with every subsequent refinement handled through conversation rather than a timeline. Testing it live on “explain recursion in a 30-second video”, the creator finds the tool generates a storyboard with GPT Image 2 and the audio track with Lyria, behind a paywall he ends up subscribing to. A second run explaining inflation in an anime style — which it chose to render in Spanish — also lands, and he rates it a “fact”.
items.author: itstundeanthony

items.title: Sell cinematic 3D restaurant menus made from one prompt
items.synopsis: The pitch is packaging AI-generated 3D menus as a premium digital product for restaurants. The workflow uploads photos of an existing menu to Google Flow, then pastes a single detailed prompt to produce the 3D effect. The output turns a flat menu into a cinematic animation with realistic detail and smooth transitions, ready to resell to multiple restaurants.
items.author: kushalfinds.ai

items.title: MiniMax H3 outputs 2K video with stereo audio in one pass
items.synopsis: China open-sourced MiniMax H3, an AI video model producing 2K video and stereo audio in a single pass. It combines video, speech, lip sync and music without stitching separate tools together. The licence permits commercial use.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Collage-style motion design with ChatGPT and Seedance
items.synopsis: A French walkthrough for producing collage-poster motion graphics using ChatGPT and Seedance 2.5. You first generate a still in ChatGPT describing the collage poster style, optionally importing a reference image to match, then ask ChatGPT to write a video prompt specifying that the animation starts on a blank canvas and reveals each collage element layer by layer. Pasting that prompt into Seedance with the reference image turns the still into a finished motion design animation.
items.author: antony_nonis

items.title: Generate a new camera angle from a single image
items.synopsis: A French demo of an AI tool that converts any single image into a new camera angle in about thirty seconds. No editing software and no cost are involved. The creator uses it to fake convincing camera movement in video projects.
items.author: jeremy_ia

items.title: Drawing a drone path on a still image in Google Flow — rated hype
items.synopsis: The premise is appealing: open Google Flow, select the OmniFlash model, upload a photo, draw red lines tracing the path you want a drone to fly, then paste a set of instructions. The creator tries it on a hiking photo of himself and the output is poor, including the model altering his skin tone for no apparent reason. Three further attempts do not improve it, and he rates the feature hype.
items.author: itstundeanthony

items.title: Claude Code edits raw footage into DaVinci Resolve
items.synopsis: The creator hands raw video to Claude Code and gets a finished edit back in one click. The result lands directly in DaVinci Resolve ready to review. The pitch is removing both the editing subscription and the hired editor from the loop.
items.author: leon.petrou

items.title: MiniMax H3 run locally against Seedance 2.0
items.synopsis: A head-to-head comparison between a free AI video model and Seedance 2.0. The team runs MiniMax H3 locally on a Dell Precision T2 tower using prompts and reference images supplied by Higgsfield. The point is showing what a local workstation delivers versus a hosted commercial model.
items.author: badxstudio

items.title: Okay, the AI filmmaking suite, renders a Forrest Gump script page straight to screen
items.synopsis: The creator dropped a single unedited page of the Forrest Gump screenplay into Okay - the AI filmmaking suite now hosted at okaywannabe.com - selected Seedance 2.5 as the renderer and hit action with no further input. The output reproduced the scene's dialogue, character blocking and the stuck leg-brace beat directly from the script text alone. He notes the suite also exposes control over characters, cast and locations, covering writing, directing, casting, editing and composing in a single AI pipeline.
items.author: jmtasu

items.title: A paid Claude skill for cartoon commercials that failed six times — rated all hype
items.synopsis: The promised workflow was simple: find the repo on GitHub, ask Claude to install the skill, then point the R-CAD skill at your website to generate a cartoon-style commercial with research and planning handled for you. In practice the skill is paywalled, and after paying, the creator's generations failed roughly six times before producing one broken output with a laptop screen rendered on the wrong side. He puts the cost at $35 wasted and rates the tool all hype — a useful negative data point on paid Claude skills.
items.author: itstundeanthony

items.title: A product ad from one image, storyboarded by AI
items.synopsis: A setup for producing a professional-looking product commercial with no ad budget. One product image is expanded into a nine-panel storyboard, then animated. The output is a finished ad ready to post.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Cutting social clips from three-hour podcasts
items.synopsis: Chat Video Pro is a plugin for extracting social clips from very long podcast recordings. It removes the subscription model, with each cut costing pennies. The creator frames it as a way for agencies to deliver more client value faster.
items.author: chatvideopro

items.title: Reviewing Claude Code video edits on a here.now page
items.synopsis: The creator edits entire videos with Claude Code, including motion graphics and captions, but found reviewing the cut miserable inside a chat window. Now Claude spins up a here.now page where the video can be watched and commented on at every timestamp needing a change. Claude then reads the feedback and builds the next version; here.now is made by Vercel and has its own agent integration.
items.author: mr.paidsocial

items.title: A full video from a single prompt with Seedance 2.5 on Morphic
items.synopsis: The creator made an entire video from one prompt using Seedance 2.5 inside Morphic Studios. The workflow is to open Morphic, select Seedance 2.5, add references, paste the prompt, and generate. The model supports 30-second single-shot videos, up to 50 references, and extending existing videos.
items.author: ai.akshu

items.title: Three rules that keep AI video out of slop territory
items.synopsis: The creator argues the fastest route to AI slop is forcing one model to do every job, and instead maps tasks to models: Soul 2.0 for realism, Soul Cinema for cinematic frames, GPT 2.0 for text-heavy images, and Nano Banana 2.0 for general editing. Second, he says to prompt as if on set with an infinite budget — name the camera, the lens, the director whose eye you want, and the film the shot should feel like, because the real bottleneck is your film vocabulary rather than the tool. Third, add organic texture such as film grain, halation, and bloom, since AI output is too clean and lacks the sensor noise and lens imperfection a real camera introduces.
items.author: buck.the.aikami

items.title: AICameraControl poses a 3D model to lock the exact camera shot for AI images
items.synopsis: The creator demonstrates using 3D models to obtain the exact shot and pose you want in AI images, starting at AICameraControl.com where you position the camera, move and rotate the model, add a second person, and adjust the pose down to individual body parts. Once the shot looks right you pick your image model, tick character sheet, and hit generate, which returns both the prompt and a reference frame to download. You then upload those into an image model such as Nano Banana Pro alongside your character sheet, and the generated image retains the pose and framing of the reference.
items.author: benkaluza.tech

items.title: yt-dlp downloads video from 1,700+ sites and pairs well with Claude
items.synopsis: The creator highlights yt-dlp as one of the most powerful and under-discussed GitHub repositories, with over 183,000 stars putting it in the top twenty repos worldwide. It downloads from more than 1,700 sites just from a URL — YouTube in 4K, whole playlists and channels in one command, Instagram reels and stories, TikTok, Facebook, X, Twitch, or audio only as MP3. It is public domain, needs no app, account, or AI credits, runs entirely locally, and can simply be handed to Claude.
items.author: alassafi.ai

items.title: Multi-angle edit from a single-camera take, via a Claude skill plus Google Omni
items.synopsis: The workflow chains two tools: a Claude skill transcribes the source video with precise timestamps and writes the entire downstream prompt automatically, then that prompt is pasted into Google Omni along with the original single-angle footage. Omni synthesises additional camera angles that were never filmed — the creator notes with some disbelief that it infers what the side of his head looks like. He flags one practical blocker, needing a VPN to Japan for access, and rates the tool a genuine “fact” rather than hype.
items.author: itstundeanthony

items.title: The EU AI Act sanctions that went live on 2 August
items.synopsis: Since Sunday 2 August, part of the EU AI Act carries active sanctions, so an app shipping AI features may already be non-compliant. The creator poses three questions to determine whether you fall in scope. A companion document is offered for bringing an app into compliance if you do.
items.author: laforet.dev

items.title: Draw a path on an image and make the camera follow it
items.synopsis: The creator demonstrates drawing directly on an image to define a path that the camera then follows through the generated shot. The technique is shown alongside a Higgsfield promotion offering Seedance 2.0 in 4K with two days of unlimited generation. A further seven days of unlimited Seedance 2.5 in 4K is announced for when that model lands on the platform.
items.author: jadheshvp

items.title: Italian AI prompt pack teased for comment delivery
items.synopsis: An Italian-language post offering a free complete prompt pack in exchange for a comment. The visible caption carries only trend hashtags and no description of the pack contents.
items.author: akapepinho

items.title: Three free AI websites for cartoon video, model comparison, and image variations
items.synopsis: The creator argues against paying for AI tools you barely use and presents three free alternatives. Between them they create cartoon videos, compare top AI models side by side, and generate dozens of image variations from a single prompt. All three are free to use.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: Wan2GP runs open-source AI video on a 6GB GPU
items.synopsis: Wan2GP is an open-source AI video generator built for people without cloud subscriptions or high-end hardware. It targets consumer GPUs, needing only about 6GB of VRAM to run. That puts it in reach of most mid-range NVIDIA cards from the past eight years.
items.author: karthikramaniai

items.title: A fabric-reveal fashion commercial from one product photo in under 60 seconds
items.synopsis: The creator contrasts clothing brands still paying for photo shoots that take weeks and cost heavily against a fabric-reveal commercial produced from a single product photo in under a minute. The process is to take your garment image, upload it to Google Flow, paste one specific prompt, and generate. The output is a premium fashion commercial showing off the garment's craftsmanship like a top-tier campaign.
items.author: keemfinity

items.title: A Spider-Man sequence generated entirely with Seedance 2.0
items.synopsis: Every web swing, gravity-defying movement, and cinematic transition in this sequence was generated with Seedance 2.0. The creator presents it as evidence the model turns simple ideas into blockbuster-style sequences. The result is described as dynamic, energetic, and unusually smooth.
items.author: fetoaciatania

items.title: Seven days of unlimited Higgsfield across Gemini OMNI Flash, Seedance 2.0 and Nano Banana Pro
items.synopsis: The creator promotes a one-day offer giving seven days of unlimited access to Higgsfield's top models. The visuals shown were made with Gemini OMNI Flash, but the plan also covers Seedance 2.0 and Nano Banana Pro. The offer advertises unlimited AI generation and unlimited cinematic video across all top models.
items.author: johngoldcreates

items.title: Overgrown, Blender's new open movie made with and about Blender
items.synopsis: The creator introduces Overgrown, a new Blender feature film made in Blender, about Blender, and by the Blender community. Beyond the film itself, the project is set to share techniques for people who want to do animation without spending a fortune. The video encourages supporting the project and cites Blender Studio, Digital Production, BlenderNation, and Reddit as sources.
items.author: keyyzako

items.title: A Vox-style explainer built by one Claude Skill
items.synopsis: The creator produced an entire Vox-style explainer video from a single prompt using only Claude Code and Higgsfield. No script was written, no scene storyboarded and After Effects never opened. One Claude Skill handled research, voiceover and every on-screen visual, and the video walks the workflow step by step.
items.author: sanji.chien

items.title: Apple-style scroll-linked product animations in four no-code steps
items.synopsis: The creator reproduces the scroll-driven animations agencies charge thousands for — where a product spins or assembles itself as you scroll — in four steps with zero code. You generate a start frame and an end frame in Google Flow, use its frames-to-video mode to animate everything in between, then run that clip through EasyGIF's video-to-image-sequence tool at 30 frames per second and download the frames as a zip. Finally you drop the whole folder into your AI coding tool and ask it to build a scroll-linked image sequence on a canvas, which she notes is exactly the trick Apple uses on its product pages.
items.author: cindiezhu

items.title: A $43k-a-month autonomous AI virtual model run from four markdown files
items.synopsis: The post analyses how a 21-year-old student built a fully autonomous AI virtual model that generated roughly $43,000 in thirty days with no creative team, camera gear, studio, or real human face, running off a single laptop at about $400 a month. The described architecture treats a subscription profile as a closed-loop software pipeline rather than manual production, applying data engineering thinking to creator-economy management. Human identity is decomposed into four modular configuration files: persona.md for the psychological profile, voice.md for the acoustic signature, flux.md for the visual anchor, and brain.md for memory and contextual behaviour during subscriber chat.
items.author: thesaar.ai

items.title: Claude + Stitch for production-ready UI systems
items.synopsis: The post tackles Claude's historical weakness at frontend work by pairing it with Stitch, Google's UI generation tool. The workflow uses Stitch to generate full UI systems and then turns them into production-ready apps with animations and connected screens. The full setup and prompts are gated behind a 'Code' comment.
items.author: sferro.ai

items.title: UI/UX Pro Max Skill + 21st.dev Magic Chat for Claude
items.synopsis: This French video shows how to turn Claude into a professional UI/UX designer capable of generating very clean websites. The setup has two steps: install the UI/UX Pro Max Skill, then add Magic Chat from 21st.dev to access a huge library of interface components. The result is pro-level web design produced directly by the agent.
items.author: danyltn

items.title: Claude 'Carousel Maker' project for viral posts
items.synopsis: The post shows how to create viral Instagram carousels in under 60 seconds using Claude. You set up a dedicated 'Carousel Maker' project, paste the provided prompt, and Claude generates the slides, hooks, and content. The prompt itself is gated behind a 'Viral' comment.
items.author: lisaworldverse

items.title: A web-design tool that hands you the prompt, not just the page
items.synopsis: The creator presents a new web-coding tool that has taken the top spot for website design, generating clean professional layouts with modern gradients and fluid animations, entirely free. What impressed him is that it does not stop at the finished result — it also gives you the exact prompt used to create it. You take that prompt straight into Cursor or a similar builder and can modify the design instantly from there.
items.author: levibecodeur

items.title: Claude Code as a full website-design replacement
items.synopsis: A designer with 10+ years of experience claims Claude Code has replaced website designers, calling it the biggest shift he has seen. Work that used to cost thousands and take days now reportedly happens in seconds. He offers a stack guide for building high-quality websites with this AI workflow.
items.author: simon.saysai

items.title: An AI site builder generating immersive 3D scroll experiences from one prompt
items.synopsis: The creator positions this new AI website builder against Lovable, arguing that other vibe-coding tools produce clean but flat landing pages. This one instead generates a fully immersive 3D scroll-based site with real depth, real motion, and interactive elements that respond as you scroll. You describe the site in a single prompt and it builds the interactive 3D experience automatically.
items.author: sebintel

items.title: NamX, a Moroccan car promising a thirty-second fill-up
items.synopsis: The post presents NamX, a Moroccan vehicle the creator says buries petrol, with a refuelling time of thirty seconds. That timing points at a removable hydrogen-capsule system rather than conventional refuelling, though the caption does not spell the mechanism out. No specifications or availability are given.
items.author: force.atlas.fa

items.title: The largest car factory in the world, at BYD
items.synopsis: A short French clip billing a BYD site as the biggest car factory on the planet. The caption is a title plus hashtags, with no figures on output, floor area or workforce. The scale claim is only supported in the video.
items.author: sciencegamingtv

items.title: Higgsfield Cinema Studio 4 ships 30+ camera-move presets
items.synopsis: Higgsfield announces Cinema Studio 4 as live, letting anyone recreate professional camera moves with AI. The workflow is to upload a source video and pick a camera-movement preset from more than thirty available. The positioning is directing your videos at a new level, with the link gated behind commenting CINEMA.
items.author: higgsfield.ai

items.title: BYD Yangwang U8 lifts itself out of sand on DiSus-P suspension
items.synopsis: The Portuguese post covers the BYD Yangwang U8, a hybrid SUV that can right itself in soft sand, clear extreme obstacles by raising its chassis and have a wheel changed from a phone app with no jack. The enabling system is named: DiSus-P intelligent suspension, which controls each wheel independently so the vehicle appears to walk on legs. It can also reportedly drive on just three wheels for up to twenty-four hours.
items.author: portal.holofote

items.title: An OSINT link pack behind a follow-and-comment gate
items.synopsis: The creator asks viewers to follow and comment OSINT to receive all of his links. Nothing in the caption names a tool or technique. It is the same lead-capture pattern as his earlier post.
items.author: carterperez.dev

items.title: Assigning Claude senior engineering roles instead of tasks
items.synopsis: The creator argues people use Claude as a simple assistant when it can work like a senior team, and that the difference lies almost entirely in how requests are framed. Rather than asking only for code or a bug fix, you assign a precise role: architect, backend engineer, frontend expert, DevOps, security, optimisation or technical lead. With the right prompts he says Claude can audit a codebase, identify risks, improve scalability, refactor an architecture or prepare a production-ready deployment.
items.author: jeremy_ia

items.title: OSINT links offered by DM in Portuguese
items.synopsis: A one-line Portuguese post offering OSINT links by direct message to anyone commenting OSINT. No tool or resource is named. The post is lead capture tagged for opsec and cybersecurity.
items.author: digocolissi

items.title: Module Shadowing poisons an AI agent running in auto mode
items.synopsis: The post walks through a concrete attack on autonomous coding agents asked to summarise an external project. The chain is explicit: the AI downloads a ZIP containing an untrusted binary decoder, its safety filter correctly refuses to execute the binary, so the agent writes its own clean Python decoder using import base64. Because base64 internally imports struct and Python searches the current folder first, the agent unwittingly executes a poisoned local struct.py, which is the Module Shadowing trap.

items.title: Router-level malware filtering with Cloudflare 1.1.1.2
items.synopsis: The creator gives a complete, copyable recipe for household-wide protection with no installation or subscription: log into the router at the address on its sticker, usually 192.168.0.1 or 192.168.1.1, open DNS settings and set the primary to 1.1.1.2 and secondary to 1.0.0.2, which is the Cloudflare malware and phishing filter. Using 1.1.1.3 and 1.0.0.3 instead adds adult-content blocking. After saving and restarting the router every device on the wifi is covered, including laptops, iPads, smart TVs, consoles and children phones.

items.synopsis: The creator presents a fashion-marketing shift in which Kling AI generates video of models wearing your own garments. He walks through the process end to end, from creating the model to the final animation, aimed at producing professional marketing video for a brand. The link is gated behind commenting mode.

items.title: Flux 1 as a free open-source rival to Midjourney
items.synopsis: The creator presents Flux 1 as a free image generator shaking Midjourney, stressing it is entirely free and open source, and points to the Pro model on Flux pro art or the Realism LORA on Fal AI. His practical advice is to alternate between Midjourney and Flux to find the right style and to iterate generously. For animation he names Dream Machine at thirty generations a day and Kling AI at sixty credits a day as the best free options, with links gated behind commenting flux.
items.author: danyltn

items.title: A claim that anyone can build an app in under a minute
items.synopsis: The creator insists literally anyone, even a parent with no technical background, can build apps in under a minute with no code. The tool is not named in the caption, though ChatGPT, OpenAI, Anthropic and Claude all appear in the hashtags. The demonstration is video-only.
items.author: brand.nat

items.title: A hyper-realistic AI clothing site behind a gate
items.synopsis: The creator teases a hyper-realistic AI clothing website and asks for an AI comment to receive it. The site is never named in the caption. Nothing can be verified from the text.

items.title: A five-step photo restoration chain in Uniconverter AI
items.synopsis: The creator argues restoring old photos for large-format print is essential for designers and that Photoshop alone does not cut it, then gives the exact sequence. Download Uniconverter AI, open the AI image enhancer, upload the image and run Old Photo Colorize then export; re-upload that result into the image upscaler at 8X and export again. Finally run Face or Auto Enhancer to render the final version.
items.author: brothersinart1

items.title: Three lines appended to every prompt for better answers
items.synopsis: The creator shares three tricks she adds to the end of every prompt when she wants seriously good answers from ChatGPT. The caption frames the recurring questions it addresses: how to get better answers, how to tailor responses to your business and what simple tweaks raise output quality. The three lines themselves are delivered in the video.
items.author: sabrina_ramonov

items.title: PDF tools worth knowing, with the list gated
items.synopsis: The creator promotes useful PDF tools and offers a list of top AI tools to anyone commenting ds. None of the PDF tools is named in the caption. The hashtags situate it in study and productivity use.

items.title: Kittl for printable designs sold to individual clients
items.synopsis: The creator argues the real advantage of AI tooling is the speed of producing visuals, which supports a system of bespoke creations per client across clothing, comic books, cards and anything printable, using kittl.com. The named tool is Kittl, and the business model is pairing those designs with content creation to drive traffic and sell. The link is gated behind commenting IDEA.
items.author: nomadatoast

items.title: Tool names promised for a one-word comment
items.synopsis: A single French line offering to send the names to anyone commenting IA. Neither the tools nor their category is stated. The post is pure lead capture.
items.author: zeynebmaxim.ai

items.title: Playground for design, plus Printify and Dream Machine
items.synopsis: The creator presents playground.com/design as a route into graphic design without technical skills, highlighting that its AI renders text correctly, long a weak point for image models, so you can talk to it and have it act as a personal designer. He then names the monetisation chain: connect printify.com to Etsy, TikTok Shop and Shopify to put designs on products and sell on autopilot. For motion he points to lumalabs.ai Dream Machine as the image animator.
items.author: nomadatoast

items.title: Cloning yourself with a HeyGen instant avatar
items.synopsis: The creator describes having fun cloning herself using the HeyGen instant avatar feature. The tool is named explicitly and the use case is a synthetic presenter version of oneself. No workflow or quality assessment is given.
items.author: imanoubou

items.title: A one-minute guide to installing Flux AI locally
items.synopsis: The creator offers a one-minute walkthrough for installing Flux AI on both Mac and PC. Flux is the open-weight image model positioned as a Midjourney alternative, and local installation is the point of the post. The steps themselves are in the video rather than the caption.
items.author: mattfarmerai

items.title: FlutterFlow named as the app-building tool
items.synopsis: The creator names the software directly in the caption: FlutterFlow, the visual builder for Flutter applications. The rest is a subscribe request with business and development hashtags. What he builds with it is shown in the video.
items.author: thomas.tavola

items.title: A law firm open-sourced 12 CC0 legal templates for AI to fill in
items.synopsis: General Legal, a law firm, published 12 attorney-written legal templates for free under CC0, among them a mutual NDA, an offer letter, a privacy policy and terms of use. The blanks are highlighted, so handing the markdown to Claude or Codex with your company name and the date is enough to have them filled in automatically. The CEO's launch post passed 600,000 views on X, but every template disclaims legal advice and the jurisdictions are narrow, with the NDA written under Delaware law and the offer letter California-only, so a lawyer should review anything that matters.
items.author: buildwithneej

items.title: Switzerland moves 3,000 federal workstations off Microsoft to open source
items.synopsis: Switzerland has begun migrating 3,000 federal government workstations to open-source office, email and desktop software, with roughly $9 million budgeted and completion targeted for the end of next year; the Swiss military cyber unit is moving faster still, aiming to replace Microsoft entirely within a month. The driver named as decisive is not licence cost but sovereignty — under US cloud law, American authorities can potentially reach data held by American companies, and Switzerland declined to run its whole government on that basis. The reel acknowledges Munich's failed 2000s Linux migration as precedent, but argues the difference now is scale: half of Europe is quietly funding open alternatives, and the software has matured.
items.author: zackshutt

items.title: Anthropic sued for fraud over Claude Max usage multipliers
items.synopsis: A news reel on a fraud suit alleging Anthropic overcharged Claude subscribers by misrepresenting how much usage the Max tiers actually deliver. According to the filing, Anthropic's own weekly estimates show the $100 Max 5× plan delivering roughly 3.5× the Pro allowance, and the $200 20× plan delivering only about six to eight times — not twenty. The suit seeks refunds for affected subscribers on the basis that a plan sold as a specific usage multiple should deliver that multiple.
items.author: lenny_builds

items.title: EIC Pathfinder: up to 4M euros of EU money, zero equity
items.synopsis: The video spotlights the EU's EIC Pathfinder programme, which grants founders up to 4 million euros that never has to be repaid and takes 0% equity. Eligible themes include AI, longevity, and clean energy. This year's round is still open with a deadline of 28 October, and the creator offers the official page to commenters.
items.author: nikolai.pov

items.title: The omni-reference trick behind a €2,094 AI animated short
items.synopsis: A client paid the creator €2,094 for an animated film despite his never having learned animation, so he generated all of it with AI — and his key point is that generating scene by scene and hoping for coherence simply does not work. You first lock the style, here borrowed from Seven Deadly Sins and Ranking of Kings, and define characters and sets before the very first generation. The technique nobody uses is omni-reference: you generate a scene, take the last frame of that generation, and make it the reference for the next scene so characters, objects and set all continue from where the previous one stopped; he recommends Seedance 2.0 for the animation and Premiere Pro for the edit.
items.author: slowdoown

items.title: Microsoft's Legal Agent in Word and the 18-month clock
items.synopsis: The Microsoft AI CEO gives white-collar jobs 18 months before AI starts automating them massively, and Microsoft has just launched its Legal Agent inside Word. The video draws a striking parallel with coding: tools like Cursor and Claude began by suggesting code and now develop autonomously. The implication is that legal work is about to follow the same automation curve.
items.author: iam_romeobach

items.title: Three files that turn Claude into a co-founder with memory and a voice
items.synopsis: Alassafi.ai describes a three-file setup: a markdown playbook encoding how he runs the company, a memory file holding every deal that persists across sessions, and a voice layer. The voice is an original built in Fish Audio's Voice Design and wired into Claude Code through their MCP with a single command, with emotion tags stacked directly into the generation input — which is why it sounds patient when the schedule holds and annoyed when it slips. He gives a concrete payoff: that morning it told him two developers were blocked and a client had not been updated.
items.author: alassafi.ai

items.title: One image into a full character bible for consistency
items.synopsis: The post tackles character consistency in AI filmmaking by turning a single input image into a complete character bible before any animation begins. The generated set covers a full-body turnaround, eight expressions, a pose sheet, costume close-ups and a HEX colour palette. Two prompt variants are offered — a fixed top row so every sheet across a cast matches, or the original free layout — both built in Picsart Flow with GPT Image 2.5.
items.author: ai.withphil

items.title: A 12-prompt pack for photoreal AI skin on a 62-year-old face
items.synopsis: The carousel presents an AI-generated portrait of a 62-year-old woman - freckles, crow's feet, crepey skin, veins on the hands - assembled from twelve deliberately sequenced prompts. Its thesis is that most AI portraits read as fake for one reason, uniformly perfect skin, whereas real skin varies by region: pores coarsen beside the nose and refine on the cheekbone, wrinkles follow the muscles, and nothing is ever entirely in focus at once. The pack ships one identity master portrait, six macro detail studies, five hand and hair shots, fix prompts for waxy skin and wig-looking hair, and the ten realism rules underpinning them.
items.author: dezinbydeepak

items.title: Reverse-engineering a real-time webcam fitting room built on Decart's Lucy 2.5 (PT)
items.synopsis: A creative engineer dissects a viral virtual fitting room that generates, live on the user's webcam, video of them wearing garments selected on the site. He identifies it as a product of Decart AI, a startup specialising in low-latency generative models, running their closed, paid Lucy 2.5 model that businesses license and wire into e-commerce or live video to swap scenery and products in real time without post-production. His point is that the capability is no longer rare: JoyAI-Video-Edit from Chinese retail giant JD is an open-source equivalent, and Krea and Vidu both ship comparable products.
items.author: leobeckerdesign

items.title: Hermes adds a Claude plugin that runs on your subscription, no API key
items.synopsis: A Hermes plugin update reconnects Claude to the agent without requiring an API key or a separate usage bill, running instead on an existing Claude subscription. Users can switch between Opus, Sonnet, Haiku and Fable with a single line, and the creator says installation takes about three minutes via one command. Hermes keeps its memory, tools, browsing and approval flow throughout, so the agent can still read files, browse the web and check its own work inside existing workflows.
items.author: aiprofitlabdaily

items.title: Checklist des micro-details qui rendent un portrait IA credible
items.synopsis: Le carrousel enumere les marqueurs concrets du realisme photographique a demander dans un prompt: pores visibles, texture naturelle de la peau, ridules, cheveux brin par brin, yeux et levres textures, asymetrie subtile et imperfections non retouchees. L'angle assume est de produire des portraits moins plastiques et plus photographiques, pour du visuel mode ou des influenceurs IA. Comme le post precedent du meme registre, il s'agit d'un pack de prompts rattache a Higgsfield Soul et delivre en DM contre le commentaire REAL, sans audio ni prompt reellement publie.
items.author: smrt.ai

items.title: Why a minimal character sheet holds an AI actor more consistently than a detailed one
items.synopsis: Adamkurtz.ai reports that the intuitive approach to character consistency — packing a reference sheet with close-ups, side profiles and full-body front and back views — actively backfired. Each additional face on the sheet gives the model another sample to average, so the character drifted between wide shots and close-ups instead of locking in. His working sheet is now three images: one close-up, one full body from behind, and one full body with no head, leaving a single face to anchor on across every shot.
items.author: adamkurtz.ai

items.title: Comment-to-unlock prompt pack for an AI image platform
items.synopsis: A carousel of AI-generated images whose caption withholds every technical detail, asking viewers to comment "REPLICAR" to receive the prompts and access to the unnamed platform behind the creations. The only concrete lead is the credited partner account @fishcreative.hq; neither the generator, the model, nor the prompt structure is disclosed in the post itself. With 909 comments against 321 likes, the engagement profile confirms the comment-gate is working as a growth mechanic rather than as a tutorial.
items.author: uendelmiranda.ia

items.title: 8K AI Realism Prompt Pack: carrousel promotionnel verrouille par commentaire
items.synopsis: Carrousel promouvant un pack de prompts oriente photorealisme 8K pour portraits generes, explicitement rattache a Higgsfield Soul dans la liste de mots-cles. La legende est presque entierement constituee d'une chaine de hashtags SEO (texture de peau, pores, headshot, influenceur IA, media synthetique) plutot que d'un contenu exploitable. Le deck de prompts lui-meme n'est delivre qu'en message prive apres avoir commente PROMPT, et le post ne comporte aucune piste audio permettant d'en extraire la substance.
items.author: luxry.ai

items.title: An open-source Chinese talking-avatar generator, with a visible skin-tone failure
items.synopsis: The reel presents a free, open-sourced alternative to HeyGen: upload a photo, drop in an audio clip, hit generate, and get a talking avatar with lip sync and facial expression. The creator's own results were poor across four attempts — distorted teeth and a generally off appearance — and noticeably better when he switched to a lighter-skinned test subject's photo, which he calls out directly with the verdict “a fact if you're white”. That makes the post as much a documented demographic-bias observation as a tool review.
items.author: itstundeanthony

items.title: Open Art turns one sentence into a directed explainer video
items.synopsis: The whole demo video began from the single prompt “explain gravity”, with every subsequent refinement handled through conversation rather than a timeline. Testing it live on “explain recursion in a 30-second video”, the creator finds the tool generates a storyboard with GPT Image 2 and the audio track with Lyria, behind a paywall he ends up subscribing to. A second run explaining inflation in an anime style — which it chose to render in Spanish — also lands, and he rates it a “fact”.
items.author: itstundeanthony

items.title: xAI Voice Agents let AI place real phone calls
items.synopsis: xAI Voice Agents move AI agents from messaging into placing actual phone calls, configured by describing the desired behaviour in plain language. You choose the script and voice, get a phone number, and test before calling for real. A real-time speech-to-speech pipeline keeps latency low and can switch languages mid-conversation, targeting lead qualification and appointment booking.
items.author: thevibefounder

items.title: Five small details that make an AI avatar read as real
items.synopsis: The creator's recurring finding is that avatar realism is never one big thing but an accumulation of tiny details. The five she watches most are skin, eyes, lighting and the small imperfections a real photograph would contain. An example prompt accompanies the breakdown so the difference is visible rather than described.
items.author: carrieparker.ai

items.title: Free open-source alternative to HeyGen avatars
items.synopsis: An open-source tool generates highly realistic AI avatars from a single photo plus an audio file. The creator positions it directly against HeyGen, with the difference being that it costs nothing. The video walks through what the tool produces before offering the links.
items.author: ia.boss.officiel

items.title: Character sheet prompts for consistent AI figures
items.synopsis: The account shares a set of character-sheet prompts for generating consistent figures across poses and views. The prompts are distributed to commenters. The account publishes regular AI prompt tips.
items.author: prompty.ai

items.title: Why AI photos look fake — and the realism layer that fixes it
items.synopsis: The creator argues that AI images look fake because of the prompt, not the model, and demonstrates with an image made in Arcads using GPT Image 2. Instead of simple descriptions he specifies exactly how a real photograph behaves — real camera settings, natural lighting, lifestyle framing — then adds a realism layer calling out visible pores, peach fuzz, baby hairs, subtle freckles, skin texture, fine wrinkles, natural lip texture, soft redness, and the tiny imperfections real cameras capture. A final pass through Skin Enhancer restores natural texture and removes the plastic AI look.
items.author: ai.akshu

items.title: Postiz: self-hosted social scheduling with an agent CLI
items.synopsis: Postiz is an open-source social media manager at roughly 30,000 GitHub stars that schedules posting across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and LinkedIn from one calendar. What Buffer cannot match is its agent CLI: you point Claude at it and tell it to schedule a week, and it drafts and queues the posts without opening a dashboard. Analytics, AI writing and a public API for n8n, Make or Zapier are included, and the self-hosted build is feature-complete and free.
items.author: brodyautomates

items.title: A free unrestricted Chinese image generator
items.synopsis: The creator presents a newly released free Chinese image tool he claims is more powerful than existing generators and ships with no content restrictions or filters. Usage is straightforward: go to the site, type your prompt, adjust a few settings and generate. He reports the output comes out sharper, more detailed and more realistic than most paid tools.
items.author: theaisurfer

items.title: InVideo Agent One Builds Full Cinematic Ads from a Brief
items.synopsis: The creator presents InVideo Agent One as a video editing agent that killed prompt engineering by following a professional production process instead of one-shot generation. From a simple creative reference it produced a GTA-style bug spray ad complete with character design, storyboards, moodboards, and game-world scenes. The link is delivered by commenting AI, positioning agentic ad production as the next step past clip generators.
items.author: nomadatoast

items.title: ElevenAgents Templates: Build an AI Agent in 60 Seconds
items.synopsis: This sponsored ElevenLabs post shows that the easiest way to build an AI agent is starting from a pre-built ElevenAgents template. Setup takes under sixty seconds and templates exist for nearly every use case, with no vibe coding required. Details are sent by DM after commenting agent.
items.author: bigpictureclub_

items.title: Pinterest to JSON prompt to Flow: an AI avatar pipeline
items.synopsis: The creator finds an avatar style he likes on Pinterest, copies the image, and asks ChatGPT to break it down in extreme detail into a JSON prompt. He copies that generated JSON prompt into a new chat, chooses image creation at 9:16, pastes it in, and gets his initial AI avatar image. That image is then uploaded into flow.com, where he sets up the image at 9:16 to carry the avatar into video generation.
items.author: dawoodzahidai

items.title: 6 Reference Boards Every AI Filmmaker Needs
items.synopsis: The carousel presents six reference boards as the underused secret weapon of AI filmmaking. They include a twelve-shot storyboard built from one image, a full character bible, a location board with time of day and weather, and a pose board for animation. The technique treats consistency and cinematic quality as a pre-production planning problem.
items.author: ai.withphil

items.title: Yamamoto Streetwear Concept with Multi-Angle Consistency
items.synopsis: The creator reimagines Bleach's Head Captain Genryusai Yamamoto in a gritty modern streetwear look. The key achievement is keeping the character's intense, battle-hardened appearance consistent across different camera angles, a task that used to be difficult. The exact prompt is offered by DM after commenting OLDMAN, and the author's sibling posts use the SeaArt platform for this workflow.
items.author: riowmartha

items.title: Seedance 2.0 + GPT Image 2.0 on SeaArt for Rukia Look
items.synopsis: The creator finally nails a realistic street-style version of Bleach's Rukia Kuchiki using the Seedance 2.0 and GPT Image 2.0 combo on SeaArt. The workflow solves the classic problem of keeping AI characters consistent across different camera angles. The full workflow and prompt are shared by DM after commenting RUKIA.
items.author: riowmartha

items.title: A free local ElevenLabs replacement with context-aware synthesis
items.synopsis: The creator declares the end of ElevenLabs, presenting a local, free and unlimited replacement he says gives nothing away to the original. It supports over 30 languages, clones your own voice, delivers high audio quality, and — the feature he stresses most — takes context into account during synthesis. It installs simply and connects to any of your solutions, which he notes suits anyone deploying voice-driven builds through Claude Code.
items.author: its.abdechan

items.title: Imperfection Detail Makes AI Avatars Read as Real
items.synopsis: The creator explains that realism in current AI portraits comes from what older models smoothed out: natural skin flaws, uneven tone, tiny freckles, and peach fuzz. The brain reads these imperfections as proof the photo is genuine. Micro-detail in the eye completes the illusion, with the full prompt set gated behind an AI comment.
items.author: bymaximade

items.title: A five-tool chain for AI avatars selling on TikTok Shop
items.synopsis: The workflow is shown as a rapid chain: take a prompt to ChatGPT, pick a reference image on Pinterest, add your image and generate; move to Nano Banana Pro, paste a second prompt and download your avatar. That avatar image plus an audio track goes into an agent that generates the talking video — demonstrated here as a perfume ad urging viewers to tap the orange cart. The finished clip is uploaded to TikTok to chase views and TikTok Shop commissions, with the full guide offered in DM.
items.author: seraphin.mp

items.title: Superscale AI Generates Human-Like Ads at Scale
items.synopsis: Superscale pitches its platform as a replacement for waiting on human influencers. Its AI creates scroll-stopping, human-like video ads in minutes, produced at scale and on demand. The value proposition targets performance marketers who need conversion-ready avatar creative without creator logistics.
items.author: getsuperscaleai

items.title: 22 design-system prompts for NotebookLM, now renamed Gemini Notebook
items.synopsis: Following a previous post on NotebookLM design prompts that drew over 20,000 comments, the creator has produced 22 more, noting in passing that Google has renamed NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook while the tool and prompts remain the same. Each prompt is a complete design system covering colours, fonts and even how the message is conveyed: Boy Band renders the deck as a 1990s album, Insert Coin as an 80s arcade game, Chalkboard as a physics lecture, Storybook as a bedtime story and Bauhaus as a 1920s art poster. You apply them inside your notebook by opening the slide deck, clicking the circle-with-arrow control, pasting the prompt into the block and hitting generate.
items.author: devinkarpes

items.title: A GitHub repo of design prompts that transform NotebookLM slide decks
items.synopsis: The creator argues NotebookLM's default slide output is merely fine, and that getting genuinely striking decks requires strong design prompts. He points to a GitHub repository holding dozens of design prompts that completely change the look of NotebookLM slides. The link is offered to commenters.
items.author: devinkarpes

items.title: Build a talking AI assistant robot with a Raspberry Pi and ChatGPT
items.synopsis: The creator demonstrates a DIY AI assistant built from a Raspberry Pi combined with ChatGPT. The reel is a short teaser for the build rather than a full walkthrough. The complete guide is hosted on the creator's MakeMindz site, linked from the caption.
items.author: makemindzz

items.title: A Raspberry Pi primer aimed at cyberdeck builders
items.synopsis: The creator put together a short primer on Raspberry Pi models specifically for cyberdeck enthusiasts. The caption states the audience and intent but does not summarise the comparison itself. The content is delivered in the video.
items.author: jstockdale

items.title: Elecrow Picrow2, a laptop-form Raspberry Pi with 20+ sensors
items.synopsis: The Portuguese post itemises the Elecrow Picrow2 specification in full: an 11.6-inch Full HD IPS screen, a detachable wireless keyboard and more than twenty sensors already integrated on the board. It also carries a built-in camera, integrated microphone and speakers, an internal rechargeable battery and a portable notebook-style chassis. GPIO ports remain exposed for projects and it is compatible with the Raspberry Pi 4 and 4B.
items.author: techtronic3dbrasil

items.title: Building an AI camera on Pi 5 with the Hailo AI HAT
items.synopsis: The creator documents assembling an AI camera step by step from a Raspberry Pi 5, a Hailo AI HAT and a Camera Module, with everything mounted and nearly ready. The Hailo HAT is the key component, providing the neural accelerator that makes on-device inference viable. The caption names the parts but not the software stack.
items.author: raspimaniax

items.title: Browser-Use: free open-source rival to AI browser agents
items.synopsis: While attention was on ChatGPT Agent and Claude Computer Use, a developer released Browser-Use, a free open-source framework that does almost the same thing. It lives on GitHub and lets an AI drive a web browser to complete tasks autonomously. The video pitches it as a game changer for virtual assistants and automation builders.
items.author: thevibefounder

items.title: ScrapeGraph AI does in free what Apify and Bright Data charge for
items.synopsis: An Italian developer released ScrapeGraph AI under an MIT licence, free forever, and it has already gathered 23,000 stars. You give it a URL and describe what you want in plain English, and the AI handles the rest — LinkedIn profiles, email addresses, Twitter accounts, Amazon, Zillow, Glassdoor — including multi-page scraping at scale. The creator's economic point is that Apify charges $49 a month and Bright Data $500, while agencies are already billing clients $5,000 per scraping project using this free tool.
items.author: criscatalyst

items.title: Scrapling: 800x faster scraper that dodges Cloudflare
items.synopsis: A French video promoting Scrapling, a scraper billed as 800 times faster than existing tools, installable in 30 seconds via Claude Code. It reportedly bypasses Cloudflare without detection, enabling claims like 10,000 leads in one night with zero banned IPs. It is presented as compatible with OpenAI Codex and other agent tooling.
items.author: just_use_ai_now

items.title: Install Scrapling in 30 seconds with Claude Code
items.synopsis: The pitch: hand Claude Code a GitHub link and 30 seconds later it has installed Scrapling, described as the most powerful scraping tool in the world. The tool claims to be 800 times faster than anything else and to get around Cloudflare protections. A free installation guide is offered to viewers who comment 'Scrap'.
items.author: baptsimard.ia

items.title: ScrapeGraph-AI threatens paid scraping platforms
items.synopsis: A developer released ScrapeGraph-AI on GitHub, an open-source LLM-powered scraping tool that has already collected over 23,000 stars. The video claims it is replacing paid scraping platforms costing around 40,000 rupees a month. It frames the project as the moment free open-source AI killed the paid web-scraping market.
items.author: thevibefounder

items.title: 'Ultimate Web Scraper' Chrome extension demo
items.synopsis: A short demo naming the Chrome extension 'Ultimate Web Scraper' as the tool being showcased. The angle is no-code data extraction directly from the browser for automation, e-commerce, and productivity use cases. Details on capabilities are thin in the caption, but the tool itself is explicitly identified.
items.author: arthur.webscraping

items.title: A GitHub repo of design prompts that transform NotebookLM slide decks
items.synopsis: The creator argues NotebookLM's default slide output is merely fine, and that getting genuinely striking decks requires strong design prompts. He points to a GitHub repository holding dozens of design prompts that completely change the look of NotebookLM slides. The link is offered to commenters.
items.author: devinkarpes

items.title: Bezos reportedly raising $100bn to buy the physical economy, not AI apps
items.synopsis: Drawing on his contact with billionaire business angels, the creator reports Jeff Bezos is in talks to raise a fund of over $100 billion — larger than most private-equity houses can raise — to acquire companies in ageing industries and rebuild them with AI. His argument is that while the media debates an AI bubble and funding rounds concentrate on new models and apps, Bezos is looking elsewhere entirely. The targets are factories, logistics, production lines, inventory, bottlenecks, underused machinery and obsolete ERP systems — the real physical economy.
items.author: ravelkel

items.title: AI5050 returns to Brussels for a fourth edition
items.synopsis: The AI5050 conference announces its fourth edition on 31 March 2026 at Hi!Site in Brussels, a single day of practical AI insight from senior experts. The promotion attached is Super Early Bird tickets bundled with two free books for a limited period. It is a local event listing rather than technical content.
items.author: ai5050conference

items.title: MacroHard : l'entreprise logicielle sans employés comme test grandeur nature
items.synopsis: Le post commente le projet MacroHard attribué à Elon Musk, une société logicielle revendiquée sans employés. L'auteur déplace l'intérêt du clin d'oeil à Microsoft vers la vraie question : savoir si une chaîne où l'IA conçoit, teste et livre peut remplacer un organigramme entier. Il souligne que le point sensible est la captation de la valeur par la propriété du capital plutôt que la prouesse technique.

items.title: Kiyosaki predicts an AI-jobs crash, with a sourcing correction
items.synopsis: The post opens by correcting a false premise, noting Robert Kiyosaki has not appeared on a widely recognised CAU podcast, though he has warned via social media and general media of a global financial crash driven partly by AI job losses. His predicted chain is that AI-driven unemployment collapses both commercial and residential real estate, producing what he calls the biggest crash in history. The media attribution is given as Central Asian University.
items.author: ai.sources

items.title: Thiel exits a 100 million dollar Nvidia stake, fuelling bubble fears
items.synopsis: NPR reports that an investment company owned by Peter Thiel has sold its entire 100 million dollar stake in Nvidia, intensifying investor concern that the AI industry is in a financial bubble. The figures given are concrete: Nvidia became the first company valued above 5 trillion dollars at the end of October, with shares up 33 percent for the year but down more than 13 percent in recent weeks. The sale follows SoftBank doing the same the previous week, and together the moves stoke fears of a speculative bubble after heavy tech investment.
